docs.x: Judge Gerald A. McHugh Jr., E.D. Pa.. docs.x: Judge Gerald A. McHugh Jr., E.D. Pa.. docs.t: Judge Gerald A. McHugh Jr. (E.D. Pa.) — Rule 16 conference
docs.x: Judge Gerald A. McHugh Jr., E.D. Pa.. Rule 16 conference: Held as soon as possible after the answer is served; if none is scheduled within a reasonable time, counsel should ask for one. It is a substantive case management conference: be ready to discuss strengths, weaknesses, essential facts, and critical documents. Produce essential documents from initial disclosures beforehand where practical, and attach critical documents to the Rule 26(f) report.

docs.x: Judge Gerald A. McHugh Jr., E.D. Pa.. Protective orders and confidentiality: Use sparingly and narrowly (Pansy). No protective or confidentiality order will be approved without language that the court reserves its inherent power to modify it and permit disclosure where the interest of justice requires. Documents forming the basis for judgment are unlikely to be protected except in exceptional circumstances.

docs.t: Judge Gerald A. McHugh Jr. (E.D. Pa.) — Arbitration, settlement, and habeas
docs.x: Judge Gerald A. McHugh Jr., E.D. Pa.. Arbitration, settlement, and habeas: No pretrial conference in arbitration cases; complete discovery before the arbitration date. With rare exceptions, no summary judgment before the arbitration hearing, and the judge may hold off resetting a continued hearing until the parties report ready. Paired with Magistrate Judge Jose Arteaga; settlement-conference referrals are strictly limited and not made in routine diversity cases. In § 2241 immigration habeas cases, the judge will consider appointing the Federal Defender for financially eligible petitioners.

docs.t: Judge Gerald A. McHugh Jr. (E.D. Pa.) — Contact and professionalism
docs.x: Judge Gerald A. McHugh Jr., E.D. Pa.. docs.x: Judge Harvey Bartle III, E.D. Pa.. docs.x: Judge Harvey Bartle III, E.D. Pa.. Hearings and conferences: No fixed days for argument or evidentiary hearings; they are scheduled ad hoc. docs.x: Judge Harvey Bartle III, E.D. Pa.. docs.x: Judge Harvey Bartle III, E.D. Pa.. docs.x: Judge Harvey Bartle III, E.D. Pa.. Courtroom conduct: Be punctual and civil. Stand to address the court; witnesses may be examined seated, and approach only with permission. Counsel should stay in the courthouse during deliberations.

docs.x: Judge Harvey Bartle III, E.D. Pa.. Criminal cases: Suppression and Starks hearings are usually held before trial. docs.x: Judge Jeffrey L. Schmehl, E.D. Pa.. Trial: Trial is set for a date certain, not a pool. Counsel conduct all civil voir dire, generally 30 minutes per side. Without agreement on admissibility, a witness may not testify about an exhibit’s content until it is admitted. Rule 50 and involuntary dismissal motions must be in writing. Unavailable witnesses testify by deposition; no delays for them. During deliberations counsel may leave but must be able to return within 10 to 15 minutes. docs.x: Judge John Frank Murphy, E.D. Pa.. Voluntary dismissal: Do not call or write chambers to mark a case settled. Use a Rule 41(a)(1)(A)(i) notice, a stipulation signed by all parties who have appeared, a Rule 41(a)(2) motion, or a docketed request for a Local Rule 41.1(b) order.

Contact and correspondence (trap): Letters or emails (Chambers_Younge@paed.uscourts.gov) only for unopposed extensions and unopposed scheduling requests; opposed extensions, contested discovery, and substantive disputes must be raised by motion. The judge does not accept carbon copies of letters to opposing counsel. Do not contact law clerks; go through Deputy Dedra Brannan or the chambers email. You may call the day before a hearing or trial to learn the courtroom. Open and read every order on the docket; the docket text may be inaccurate, and counsel are responsible for the actual content.

docs.t: Judge John Milton Younge (E.D. Pa.) — Hearings and conferences
docs.x: Judge John Milton Younge, E.D. Pa.. Hearings and conferences: No set days for argument or hearings; they are scheduled ad hoc, and argument is heard only if the judge thinks it will help. Scheduling, case management, and similar conferences are often by video or phone, with connection details emailed in advance.

docs.t: Judge John Milton Younge (E.D. Pa.) — Motions (trap)
docs.x: Judge John Milton Younge, E.D. Pa.. Motions (trap): Motion practice follows Local Civil Rule 7.1 except as stated. A proposed order must be filed with every motion and every response, titled “Order,” with no attorney name or address (add “File Under Seal” to the caption if it is to be sealed). Replies and sur-replies, limited to issues raised in the opposition or reply, may be filed within 7 days of service and are limited to 10 pages. Courtesy copies only when chambers asks (for voluminous filings), marked, tabbed, and bound to lie flat, by mail or hand delivery. Searchable (OCR) briefs are encouraged.

docs.t: Judge John Milton Younge (E.D. Pa.) — Summary judgment (trap)
docs.x: Judge John Milton Younge, E.D. Pa.. Summary judgment (trap): The movant files a separate Statement of Undisputed Material Facts in numbered paragraphs. The opponent files a separate statement responding paragraph by paragraph (admitted or disputed) and may add numbered Additional Disputed Material Facts; the movant must respond to those within 7 business days. Facts not addressed are deemed admitted, facts without pinpoint record citations are not considered, and noncompliant summary judgment papers will be stricken.

docs.t: Judge John Milton Younge (E.D. Pa.) — Rule 16 conference and discovery (trap)
docs.x: Judge John Milton Younge, E.D. Pa.. Rule 16 conference and discovery (trap): Start discovery as soon as the order scheduling the Rule 16 conference arrives. Hold the Rule 26(f) meeting at least 10 days before the conference and, without exception, file the joint 26(f) report at least 5 business days before. Be ready to discuss settlement and consent to a magistrate judge. The 26(f) form says discovery should normally end no more than 120 days after the Rule 16 conference and expects simultaneous expert reports; the policies say the judge generally permits 3 to 6 months. Cases go to a trial pool or a date certain only after discovery is complete and dispositive motions are filed. Discovery disputes: motion under L.R. 26.1(b) with the 26.1(f) certification, a proposed order, and a brief of no more than 10 pages; response limited to 10 pages. The court may rule, confer, refer to a magistrat

docs.t: Judge John Milton Younge (E.D. Pa.) — Continuances and settlement
docs.x: Judge John Milton Younge, E.D. Pa.. Continuances and settlement: The judge is extremely reluctant to continue trial dates, especially absent diligence; discovery extensions need good cause. Settlement conferences usually go to a magistrate judge; the judge may instead refer a case to a settlement master at the parties’ cost.

docs.t: Judge John Milton Younge (E.D. Pa.) — Pretrial (trap)
docs.x: Judge John Milton Younge, E.D. Pa.. Pretrial (trap): About 3 weeks before trial (by court-set date): joint voir dire, a joint brief statement of the case, joint jury instructions, a joint verdict sheet, motions in limine, and the pretrial memorandum, all emailed to chambers in Word (PDF not acceptable). In limine responses are due in 5 business days. Points for charge are numbered, one per page, with authority (Third Circuit models where applicable); where the parties disagree, give each side’s version and rationale. The pretrial memo is due 7 days before the final pretrial conference, where the case gets a date certain or a trial pool. Exhibits: one copy and two schedules about 3 weeks before trial, tabbed in binders, plus another copy at trial. Objections to witnesses and exhibits are also due about 3 weeks before, after conferring. Give written notice of deposition use 1 month before

docs.t: Judge John Milton Younge (E.D. Pa.) — Injunctions and non-jury trials
docs.x: Judge John Milton Younge, E.D. Pa.. Injunctions and non-jury trials: The judge rarely grants ex parte TROs and requires all counsel at the TRO conference unless urgency prevents notice. Expedited discovery is usually allowed for preliminary relief, PI and permanent injunction hearings may be combined, and proposed findings and conclusions are required. Non-jury trials: file a stipulation of uncontested facts, and each party submits proposed findings and conclusions.

docs.t: Judge John Milton Younge (E.D. Pa.) — Trial and courtroom conduct (trap)
docs.x: Judge John Milton Younge, E.D. Pa.. Trial and courtroom conduct (trap): Court convenes at 9:30 a.m. and may sit to 5 p.m. or later. Counsel conduct civil voir dire with minimal oversight; the judge conducts criminal voir dire. No speaking objections and no continuing objections; state every objection in a word or phrase. Only one attorney per party may examine a witness. Stand to address the court and jury, approach witnesses only with permission, and never approach the jury to hand out exhibits. Exhibits are generally admitted at the close of evidence. Be ready to close immediately after the evidence; time limits for openings and closings are discussed in advance. Object to jury charges on the record at the charging conference. Stay within 15 minutes of the courthouse during deliberations.

docs.t: Judge John Milton Younge (E.D. Pa.) — Criminal cases (trap)
docs.x: Judge John Milton Younge, E.D. Pa.. Criminal cases (trap): Pretrial motions (including Starks, Daubert, and suppression) are due by the scheduling-order deadline and never later than 6 weeks before trial, with responses in 7 days; hearings are at least 30 days before trial, and findings and conclusions are due 10 days after. Rule 404(b) motions with a proposed limiting instruction are due by the same deadline; responses in 5 business days. Trial continuance motions must be filed at least 14 days before trial, with a Speedy Trial Act proposed order containing ends-of-justice findings and a signed speedy trial waiver; no letter requests. Joint points for charge and verdict form and the government’s trial memorandum are due 3 weeks before trial, in Word by email. Plea memoranda and agreements are due 10 days before the plea date. docs.t: Judge Joshua Wolson (E.D. Pa.) — Emails, stipulations, and proposed orders (trap)
docs.x: Judge Joshua Wolson, E.D. Pa.. Emails, stipulations, and proposed orders (trap): Contrary to Local Civil Rule 5.1.2(9), email all stipulations and proposed orders to chambers as Word documents instead of filing them on the docket. Emails need the case name and docket number in the subject line plus required keywords: “request for extension,” “request for continuance,” “proposed order,” “stipulation,” “26(f) report,” “page limits,” “deposition scheduling,” or “settlement status.” Letters by email are only for routine matters with no expected opposition; send responsive letters only on request.

docs.t: Judge Joshua Wolson (E.D. Pa.) — Filing and courtesy copies (trap)
docs.x: Judge Joshua Wolson, E.D. Pa.. Filing and courtesy copies (trap): File each exhibit as a separate, descriptively named ECF document; a single “Exhibits” file will be struck. Exhibits must be text-searchable (OCR scans). Submit full-size transcript pages (no miniscripts) with a cover page and only relevant pages. Don’t attach pleadings from this or other federal cases; cite them, but do attach state or foreign pleadings not on Westlaw or Lexis. Courtesy copies are required only for sealed filings and motions with more than 5 exhibits: email the as-filed versions to WolsonCourtesyCopy@paed.uscourts.gov (caption, filing title, and ECF number in the subject), as separate files or with a cover sheet. No paper, Dropbox, or FTP.

docs.t: Judge Joshua Wolson (E.D. Pa.) — Meet and confer and Rule 12 premotion process (trap)
docs.x: Judge Joshua Wolson, E.D. Pa.. Meet and confer and Rule 12 premotion process (trap): Every meet-and-confer obligation requires a verbal conversation (in person, video, or phone); letters and emails don’t count. Before any Rule 12 motion, confer substantively by phone or in person and offer a chance to cure, at least 1 week before the due date (in removed cases, within 3 business days of assignment). If unresolved, email a joint letter of up to 5 single-spaced pages stating each issue and each side’s position by the response deadline (extended 7 days in removed cases). The judge then holds a premotion conference and, if needed, sets briefing. Not applicable in pro se cases.

docs.t: Judge Joshua Wolson (E.D. Pa.) — Motions and briefs (trap)
docs.x: Judge Joshua Wolson, E.D. Pa.. Motions and briefs (trap): Double-spaced, at least 12-point proportional font, footnotes in the same size, 1-inch margins; table of contents if over 10 pages; cite docketed documents by ECF number. Substantive arguments in footnotes will not be considered or deemed preserved. Limits: opening and opposition 25 pages (or 8,750 words with certification); replies 10 pages or 3,500 words; sur-replies 7 pages or 2,450 words. Requests to exceed must reach the judge at least 7 days before the due date, by letter stating opposing counsel’s position. Replies and sur-replies only when necessary, on new issues, within 7 days of the prior filing; no further submissions except notice of new binding authority. Co-parties must file jointly absent clear conflicts, within one party’s page limit. No incorporation by reference. Don’t respond to reconsideration motions unless o

docs.t: Judge Joshua Wolson (E.D. Pa.) — Summary judgment
docs.x: Judge Joshua Wolson, E.D. Pa.. Summary judgment: File a single jointly prepared consolidated statement of facts and a joint exhibit set. The movant serves (not files) numbered facts with cites at least 28 days before the deadline; respondents serve responses under each paragraph, plus additional facts, at least 14 days before; the movant may reply, then files it all with the motion. Cross-movants may file separate statements but share one exhibit set. Not applicable when a party is a pro se prisoner. Expert-inadmissibility arguments must be raised in a separate, contemporaneous Daubert motion. No summary judgment in bench-trial cases without leave sought by letter within 7 days after discovery closes.

docs.t: Judge Joshua Wolson (E.D. Pa.) — Rule 16 conference and discovery (trap)
docs.x: Judge Joshua Wolson, E.D. Pa.. Rule 16 conference and discovery (trap): Lead trial counsel must attend the Rule 16 conference in person, must take part in the 26(f) conference (or the attendee becomes lead counsel), and must attend all proceedings and give opening and closing at trial absent a written client request. Email the joint 26(f) report on the judge’s form at least 7 days before the conference; the form requires key facts, critical documents, realistic discovery numbers, and deposition dates set aside, and warns that noncompliant submissions will be struck. Pending motions do not stay 26(f) or Rule 16 obligations, and discovery should start as soon as the Rules allow; stays are granted only in extraordinary circumstances, on request at the Rule 16 conference. Expect expert discovery to run before, not after, the discovery close; initial disclosures at least 1 business day before

docs.t: Judge Joshua Wolson (E.D. Pa.) — Sealing and protective orders (trap)
docs.x: Judge Joshua Wolson, E.D. Pa.. Sealing and protective orders (trap): Follow Avandia. Move to seal when filing the material (or earlier), email chambers copies of everything proposed for sealing, and file a public redacted version unless it would be unreadable, plus an unredacted highlighted version. Parties must cooperate on material an opponent marked confidential or risk costs; more than 10 sealing designations in one submission will likely go to a special master at the parties’ cost. Protective orders and confidentiality agreements require a motion meeting Avandia and Pansy; stipulated proposed orders are not accepted in place of a motion.

docs.t: Judge Joshua Wolson (E.D. Pa.) — Extensions, settlement, and arbitration
docs.x: Judge Joshua Wolson, E.D. Pa.. Extensions, settlement, and arbitration: Continuances of trial and court events only in extreme circumstances; other extensions for good cause, by emailed letter stating the opponent’s position, at least 7 days before the deadline. Pro hac vice motions without the fee are denied, and admittees must register for CM/ECF within 7 days or lose admission. The judge will not retain jurisdiction to enforce confidential settlements; put the agreement on the docket or its material terms in the stipulation of dismissal. Arbitration-track cases: usually no pretrial conference, all discovery done before the arbitration date, and no added discovery or summary judgment after a trial de novo demand.

docs.t: Judge Joshua Wolson (E.D. Pa.) — Pretrial and trial
docs.x: Judge Joshua Wolson, E.D. Pa.. Pretrial and trial: Pretrial memoranda must include L.R. 16.1 matters plus a position on trial time limits. No more than 5 motions in limine per party absent leave. Joint jury instructions, each numbered on a separate page with authority, noting changes to model instructions. The judge conducts voir dire with individual sidebar questioning; cause challenges follow each juror. Examine and address the jury from the podium; approach witnesses without asking. No speaking objections; one attorney per side per witness, opening, or summation. Leave is required to leave the courthouse during deliberations. Bench trials: direct expert testimony by affidavit, with live cross and redirect only. Courtroom 12-B; arrange technology runs with the deputy in advance. Junior lawyers are encouraged to argue, with a second lawyer allowed if requested in advance.

docs.t: Judge Joshua Wolson (E.D. Pa.) — Criminal and habeas
docs.x: Judge Joshua Wolson, E.D. Pa.. Suppression, Starks, and Daubert hearings typically at least 14 days before trial. Government trial memorandum at least 7 days before trial; guilty plea memorandum at least 3 business days before the change of plea hearing. Sentencing motions and memoranda at least 7 days before sentencing, responses at least 3 days before; continuances over 90 days not considered absent extraordinary circumstances, with joint status updates every 45 days after any further continuance. docs.t: Judge Juan Ramon Sánchez (E.D. Pa.) — Chambers contact and courtesy copies
docs.x: Judge Juan Ramon Sánchez, E.D. Pa.. Chambers contact and courtesy copies: Phone, letter, email, or fax for scheduling and non-substantive matters only, through Courtroom Deputy Nancy DeLisle (267-299-7789). Emails go to chambers with a copy to Ms. DeLisle, include case name and number in the subject, and are copied to all counsel. Courtesy copies are not required unless requested, but for filings with over 50 pages of exhibits a tabbed courtesy copy is encouraged. Stipulations and consent decrees must be signed by all counsel. Exhibits must be separately numbered, descriptively titled attachments, or accompanied by an index if filed as one PDF.

docs.t: Judge Juan Ramon Sánchez (E.D. Pa.) — Extensions and continuances (trap)
docs.x: Judge Juan Ramon Sánchez, E.D. Pa.. Extensions and continuances (trap): Extension and continuance requests go to the judge by letter (email is fine), stating opposing counsel’s position and effect on other deadlines; no formal motion is needed. Unopposed requests are not automatically granted. Extensions of the dispositive-motion deadline or trial pool date are granted only in very limited circumstances, and requests to continue Rule 16 conferences are discouraged.

docs.t: Judge Juan Ramon Sánchez (E.D. Pa.) — Rule 16 conference (trap)
docs.x: Judge Juan Ramon Sánchez, E.D. Pa.. Rule 16 conference (trap): Usually by telephone. Lead trial counsel must participate and have entered an appearance (unless a substitution is pre-approved); if lead counsel is pro hac vice, local counsel must also participate, and pro hac vice applications must be approved beforehand. Email the Joint Rule 16 Conference Information Report to chambers no later than one day before the conference. Parties who skip a meaningful Rule 26(f) meeting have no voice at the conference and may be sanctioned. File threshold motions before the conference and be ready to argue them, and be ready to discuss settlement with the judge or magistrate judge right after. Expect a final pretrial conference about a month after dispositive motions and a trial pool about a week later.

docs.t: Judge Juan Ramon Sánchez (E.D. Pa.) — Motions and page limits (trap)
docs.x: Judge Juan Ramon Sánchez, E.D. Pa.. Motions and page limits (trap): A motion and supporting memorandum together may not exceed 15 pages; oppositions 15 pages. Times New Roman 12-point (footnotes too), one-inch margins, double-spaced; cite exhibit, page, and line. Replies may be filed without leave only for summary judgment or other dispositive motions (with leave for others), up to 7 pages, within 7 days of the opposition. Sur-replies need leave for good cause and are limited to 5 pages. Before a Rule 12 motion on a curable defect, certify that opposing counsel had a chance to cure. The judge warns of Rule 11 sanctions for filings without factual basis and encourages bringing clients to argument on dispositive motions.

docs.t: Judge Juan Ramon Sánchez (E.D. Pa.) — Summary judgment
docs.x: Judge Juan Ramon Sánchez, E.D. Pa.. Summary judgment: File a separate, concise numbered statement of material facts, each with exhibit, page, and line citations; unsupported facts are not considered. The opponent responds paragraph by paragraph, citing the record for any dispute, and adds additional facts in numbered paragraphs; uncontroverted facts are deemed admitted. Submit entire deposition transcripts as exhibits.

docs.t: Judge Juan Ramon Sánchez (E.D. Pa.) — Discovery
docs.x: Judge Juan Ramon Sánchez, E.D. Pa.. Discovery: Exhaust all efforts first. Then email chambers a letter briefly outlining the dispute, certifying good-faith efforts, and requesting a phone conference; do not file a discovery motion until the conference is held. Expert depositions must be completed before the dispositive-motion deadline.

docs.t: Judge Juan Ramon Sánchez (E.D. Pa.) — Settlement, injunctions, and sealing
docs.x: Judge Juan Ramon Sánchez, E.D. Pa.. Settlement, injunctions, and sealing: Early referral to a magistrate judge is encouraged, or a mediator from the court’s list. Notify chambers immediately on settlement and seek dismissal under Local Rule 41.1; papers must be done before trial or the case will be called. TRO requests get an immediate conference with all counsel unless urgency prevents notice; expedited discovery is generally allowed for injunctions. Sealed filings need a motion for leave under Local Rule 5.1.2; highly sensitive documents follow the court’s January 22, 2021 standing order.

docs.t: Judge Juan Ramon Sánchez (E.D. Pa.) — Final pretrial and trial submissions (trap)
docs.x: Judge Juan Ramon Sánchez, E.D. Pa.. Final pretrial and trial submissions (trap): Cases are usually assigned a two-week trial pool, with 72 hours’ notice where possible (never less than 24). A pending summary judgment motion must be argued at the final pretrial conference. Exchange deposition designations at least one week before the final pretrial conference and counter-designations 3 days before; submit written objections by letter, with transcripts, one day before. Submit pretrial memoranda, a neutral statement of facts, joint voir dire (no more than 15 questions, disputes highlighted), and joint points for charge and verdict slip (one instruction per page, disputes highlighted), filed on the docket and emailed to chambers in Word. Third Circuit models preferred.

docs.t: Judge Juan Ramon Sánchez (E.D. Pa.) — Trial practice (trap)
docs.x: Judge Juan Ramon Sánchez, E.D. Pa.. Trial practice (trap): Testimony starts at 9 a.m.; raise issues 8 to 9 a.m., at breaks, or after the jury leaves, since sidebars are discouraged. Examine from the lectern, give a next-day witness list at the end of each day, and don’t run out of witnesses. One joint, sequentially numbered exhibit set (defendant’s numbers continue from plaintiff’s), with a table of contents including “Admitted” and “Not Admitted” columns; 2 copies for the court and one for witnesses. Admitted exhibits go to the jury on a court laptop via a USB drive with a hyperlinked joint exhibit chart and PDF, video, and audio folders. Openings or closings over 30 minutes need permission; closing is limited to 30 minutes including rebuttal, and plaintiff must reserve rebuttal time or waive it. Objections are one or two words; recross is generally allowed only on new matter from redir

docs.t: Judge Juan Ramon Sánchez (E.D. Pa.) — Criminal cases (trap)
docs.x: Judge Juan Ramon Sánchez, E.D. Pa.. Criminal cases (trap): Continuance and extension requests go by motion with proposed order; trial continuance motions are due at least 14 days before trial with a Speedy Trial Act ends-of-justice finding. Upon filing a motion, say whether testimony will be offered and how long. Plea papers go to chambers 2 days before the plea hearing if possible, and plea memoranda must also be filed. The government must give Rule 404(b) notice, with a proposed limiting instruction, before the final pretrial conference. Sentencing continuances are for good cause only and never more than 90 days at a time. Sentencing motions are due 14 days before (responses 7 days); simultaneous sentencing memoranda one week before (responses 3 days). PSR objections may not be raised first in a memorandum.

docs.t: Judge Kai Scott (E.D. Pa.) — AI disclosure (trap)
docs.x: Judge Kai Scott, E.D. Pa.. AI disclosure (trap): Any attorney or pro se party who used AI in any way to prepare a filing must disclose that in a clear factual statement and certify that every citation to law or the record was verified (August 2026 policies). The March 3, 2025 standing order, narrower in scope, also requires naming the specific generative AI program used when it helped with citations of legal authority.

docs.t: Judge Kai Scott (E.D. Pa.) — Contact and filing format
docs.x: Judge Kai Scott, E.D. Pa.. Contact and filing format: Email chambers for general inquiries. Judicial Assistant Tayai Lester (267-299-7590) handles civil scheduling; Courtroom Deputy Sue Flaherty (267-299-7598) handles criminal matters and trial logistics. Faxes and mail are strongly discouraged. Case communications go by ECF filing; email only for unanticipated schedule changes less than 7 business days before a deadline, private personal or medical scheduling issues, or settlement notice. File searchable PDFs. Everything is 12-point, generally double-spaced, with 1-to-1.5-inch justified margins (26(f) reports, one-page motions, and proposed orders may be single-spaced). Briefs over 25 pages need a table of contents. Courtesy copies only for sealed filings or filings with large attachments (over 50 pages of exhibits or 5 or more exhibits), as a tabbed binder with an exhibit index.

docs.t: Judge Kai Scott (E.D. Pa.) — Continuances: no stipulations (trap)
docs.x: Judge Kai Scott, E.D. Pa.. Continuances: no stipulations (trap): Changes to operative deadlines may not be filed as stipulations; file a joint unopposed motion with a proposed order. Oppositions to opposed continuance motions are due in 3 business days. Joint discovery continuances are generally granted if made at least 7 business days ahead and they don’t alter key motion deadlines or trial. Changes to argued motion deadlines or trial dates are seldom granted and need good cause at least 14 business days ahead.

docs.t: Judge Kai Scott (E.D. Pa.) — Motions (trap)
docs.x: Judge Kai Scott, E.D. Pa.. Motions (trap): Dispositive motions and memoranda are limited to 25 pages; seek leave for more at least 3 business days before the deadline (unless the overage is only from embedded pictures or charts, which you must certify). Co-parties must file joint motions unless their positions conflict. One reply, up to 10 pages, within 14 business days of the opposition; anything further needs leave, rarely granted. Threshold motions (dismiss, transfer, add or substitute parties) are due 7 days before the Rule 16 conference (7 business days per the 26(f) section), and may be argued there. Oral argument only if it would help; junior attorneys are encouraged to argue. Bring 2 copies of any physical exhibits. Amended pleadings must show changes by comments or track changes; one amendment as of right, then leave.

docs.t: Judge Kai Scott (E.D. Pa.) — Summary judgment and Daubert (trap)
docs.x: Judge Kai Scott, E.D. Pa.. Summary judgment and Daubert (trap): File the statement of facts as a separate document with the motion: either joint stipulated facts or the movant’s proposed undisputed facts, in numbered paragraphs with pinpoint cites to exhibit page and line. The nonmovant responds to each fact (undisputed, disputed with cites, or immaterial with cites) and may add facts, which the movant answers in a separate document. Statements must be brief and nonargumentative. A joint appendix is encouraged; otherwise the responder cites the movant’s appendix where possible. Any summary judgment argument that expert testimony is inadmissible must come with a contemporaneous Daubert motion. Daubert motions are due no later than 7 days before the final pretrial conference.

docs.t: Judge Kai Scott (E.D. Pa.) — Rule 26(f) and Rule 16 (trap)
docs.x: Judge Kai Scott, E.D. Pa.. Rule 26(f) and Rule 16 (trap): Meet in person or by video (email is insufficient) at least 14 business days before the Rule 16 conference, and submit the judge’s 26(f) form, with key documents attached, at least 7 business days before. Flawed reports are returned; parties not participating in good faith have no voice at the conference. Rule 16 conferences are in person in chambers. Lead counsel must attend; if counsel lack full settlement authority, someone with it must be available by phone throughout. Bring irreversible conflicts in the 3 to 9 months after the conference. Begin discovery on notice of the Rule 16 conference; pending motions are no excuse. Explain any proposed discovery period over 90 days. Expert reports are normally simultaneous.

docs.t: Judge Kai Scott (E.D. Pa.) — Discovery and sealing
docs.x: Judge Kai Scott, E.D. Pa.. No sealed filings without leave except in emergencies; sealing requires good cause or a pre-litigation confidentiality agreement, and parties can’t stipulate around good cause. Sealing orders must reserve the court’s power to modify and permit disclosure. File a redacted copy within 14 days of a sealing order.

docs.t: Judge Kai Scott (E.D. Pa.) — Injunctions
docs.x: Judge Kai Scott, E.D. Pa.. Injunctions: The judge tries to hold a prompt conference after service. A party seeking pretrial injunctive relief should be ready for a hearing within a month, or seek expedited discovery first.

docs.x: Judge Mark A. Kearney, E.D. Pa.. Objections by rule number or one word only; one attorney per witness; no conferring with a witness during testimony. Joint chronological exhibit book with two copies for the judge at voir dire (unless all electronic); motions to admit exhibits at the close of each case-in-chief. Plaintiff must email all admitted exhibits to chambers before the verdict. Counsel must stay in the courthouse during deliberations and return within 10 minutes of a call.

Government guilty plea memorandum at least 2 days before the plea hearing, emailed in Word. Lead trial counsel must attend the final pretrial conference, where in limine motions (preferably written and filed well in advance) are heard and video deposition objections must be resolved, with tabbed transcripts. The court may impose time limits. Joint substantive jury instructions and verdict forms are due on the scheduling-order date, plus each party’s own on disputed issues, with Word copies to chambers. Exhibits: Prepare a single set of exhibits numbered sequentially regardless of which side offers them, with no duplicates, in binders with a table of contents (Exhibit/Bates number, description, Stipulations, Introduced, Admitted); two copies for the court. A witness may not testify to an exhibit’s content until it is admitted unless the parties agree. At the close of evidence, give the court a thumb drive of admitted exhibits only, for the jury.

docs.t: Judge Wendy Beetlestone (E.D. Pa.) — Trial and courtroom conduct (trap)
docs.x: Judge Wendy Beetlestone, E.D. Pa.. Trial and courtroom conduct (trap): Trials usually have a date certain; court may sit from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. or later. The judge conducts voir dire with party input and rarely allows juror notes. The jury is usually charged before closings. Stay within 10 minutes of the courthouse during deliberations. Phones must be off, not silent; violators risk confiscation. No food, drink, or gum. Rise to address the court; approach witnesses only with leave; don’t confer with a testifying witness until excused; sidebars are discouraged. Seating or extra-table requests go to the deputy at least 1 week before trial. Give opposing counsel and the court the next day’s witness list in order, and don’t run out of witnesses. Only one attorney per witness or point.

docs.x: Judge Ana C. Reyes, D.D.C.. Summary judgment (trap): Local Civil Rule 7(h) is strictly enforced. The movant’s Statement of Material Facts Not in Dispute is a two-column table with one undisputed fact per numbered row in the left column, with record cites, and the movant must promptly send an editable copy to the opponent. The opponent files a Counter-Statement of Disputed Facts answering each row in the right column (admitted or denied, with cites, specifying partial admissions), then adds its additional facts and its list of genuinely disputed material facts in consecutively numbered rows at the end, and sends an editable copy back. docs.t: Judge Tanya Chutkan (D.D.C.) — Civil pretrial statement (trap)
docs.x: Judge Tanya Chutkan, D.D.C.. Plaintiff files one Joint Pretrial Statement under LCvR 16.5; separate statements are stricken sua sponte. Persons with settlement authority must attend the pretrial conference or be available by phone. Format: double-spaced, 12-point Times New Roman, Word, margins of at least 1 inch. Deliver two hard copies in separate tabbed three-ring binders to the courtroom deputy and email a copy to chambers by the court-set deadlines. Unlisted witnesses (other than impeachment) and unlisted exhibits are excluded; use the judge’s exhibit list form. Exhibits are presumed authentic and admissible absent a specific written objection in the statement, and undisclosed objec

docs.t: Judge Tanya Chutkan (D.D.C.) — Civil jury materials and motions in limine (trap)
docs.x: Judge Tanya Chutkan, D.D.C.. Civil jury materials and motions in limine (trap): Jury cases: any waiver, objections or additions to the judge’s standard voir dire (agreed and disputed, with objections under each), proposed instructions each on a new page with source citations and agreed and disputed sets, and a verdict form with a date and foreperson signature line; an objection to the verdict form needs a proposed alternative. Bench trials need detailed proposed findings and conclusions. One omnibus motion in limine per side, up to 20 pages, oppositions up to 15 pages, and no reply without leave; motions should be fully briefed when the Joint Pretrial Statement is filed. Rule 404(b) evidence must be disclosed by the set date. Unopposed motions and unanswered arguments may be treated as conceded.

docs.t: Judge Tanya Chutkan (D.D.C.) — Criminal pretrial (trap)
docs.x: Judge Tanya Chutkan, D.D.C.. Criminal pretrial (trap): Trial begins at 9:30 a.m. in Courtroom 9. The pretrial conference is in person unless the parties jointly request videoconference, and the court rules there on pretrial motions and exhibit objections where possible. Chambers sends the judge’s standard voir dire; objections and additions are due by the set date. File proposed jury instructions and verdict form on ECF, jointly where possible; list Redbook pattern instructions by number and submit special instructions verbatim with authority, marking agreed and disputed ones. Brady material is disclosed on a rolling basis and Giglio (including Lewis material) as soon as practicable; on the witness-list exchange date the government must also produce any remaining Brady or Giglio material for each listed witness. Security-based withholding of witness names must be raised in camera. Exhibi

docs.t: Judge Timothy J. Kelly (D.D.C.) — Contact with chambers (trap)
docs.x: Judge Timothy J. Kelly, D.D.C.. Contact with chambers (trap): No telephone calls to chambers except as the order authorizes; in extraordinary circumstances or emergencies, counsel may call jointly by conference call. No ex parte communication, including through law clerks, and chambers gives no legal advice. Scheduling inquiries go to the courtroom deputy, Katrina Harris (Katrina_Harris@dcd.uscourts.gov, 202-354-3495).

docs.t: Judge Timothy J. Kelly (D.D.C.) — Courtesy copies (trap)
docs.x: Judge Timothy J. Kelly, D.D.C.. Courtesy copies (trap): For any summary judgment motion, or any motion whose combined submissions from both sides (with exhibits) exceed 100 pages, the moving party delivers two binders of all motion papers to chambers when the reply is filed; on cross-motions, the initial movant supplies the full set. Copies keep the CM/ECF headers and are three-hole punched, double-sided, tabbed, and indexed. Hand deliveries go to the loading dock, not chambers. Copies are unredacted, with publicly redacted or sealed portions highlighted. Pro se parties are excused.

docs.t: Judge Timothy J. Kelly (D.D.C.) — Summary judgment (trap)
docs.x: Judge Timothy J. Kelly, D.D.C.. Summary judgment (trap): LCvR 7(h)(1) is strictly enforced, and nonconforming statements may be stricken; the court cites Jackson v. Finnegan, 101 F.3d 145 (D.C. Cir. 1996). Statements are two-column tables: the movant’s “Statement of Material Facts Not in Dispute” (left column, one cited fact per numbered row); the opponent’s “Counter-Statement of Disputed Facts” (movant’s facts on the left, admitted or denied with record citations on the right, partial admissions specified, and additional facts in consecutively numbered rows at the end of the right column); and the movant’s “Reply to Counter-Statement of Disputed Facts” answering the additional facts. Sample statements are attached to the order. After filing its statement, each side promptly gives the other an editable electronic copy.

docs.t: Judge Timothy J. Kelly (D.D.C.) — Extensions and rescheduling (trap)
docs.x: Judge Timothy J. Kelly, D.D.C.. Extensions and rescheduling (trap): Extensions are discouraged and granted only on motion, never by stipulation, filed at least four days before the deadline (or explaining why not). The motion states the original deadline, time requested, prior extensions for each party, good cause, effect on other deadlines, a proposed schedule for affected deadlines after consulting opposing counsel, and the opponent’s position under LCvR 7(m). Any opposition is due by 5:00 p.m. the next business day. Rescheduling hearings is discouraged: meet and confer, then move at least one week before the hearing (or explain why not), showing good cause and proposing four alternative dates and times convenient for all parties. Weather or emergency closures are rescheduled by the courtroom deputy.

docs.t: Judge Timothy J. Kelly (D.D.C.) — Non-dispositive motions, protective orders, and sealing (trap)
docs.x: Judge Timothy J. Kelly, D.D.C.. Non-dispositive motions, protective orders, and sealing (trap): Non-dispositive motions without the LCvR 7(m) statement, and pro hac vice motions missing LCvR 83.2(d) information, may be denied. Protective-order motions attach the proposed order and explain good cause under Rule 26(c). Motions to seal (LCvR 5.1(h)) must address the Hubbard factors, propose redactions or explain why they are impracticable, and attach each document as a separate exhibit. A protective order alone does not justify sealing. With proposed redactions, also file an unredacted copy with the proposed redactions highlighted.

docs.t: Judge Timothy J. Kelly (D.D.C.) — Filing, pleadings, and scheduling
docs.x: Judge Timothy J. Kelly, D.D.C.. Filing, pleadings, and scheduling: File electronically in text-searchable PDF (OCR for paper-only exhibits); title documents clearly and file exhibits separately. Last-minute technical problems are not necessarily good cause for an extension. Amended or proposed amended pleadings need a redline against the original. Plaintiff serves the standing order on all parties; a removing defendant refiles the complaint and any answer as a supplement to the notice of removal and refiles pending motions (Rule 81(c)(2)). After the answer, the court sets an initial scheduling conference and orders a joint LCvR 16.3(c) report. Proceedings are in Courtroom 11; for telephonic proceedings, call the courtroom deputy at least one business day ahead.

docs.t: Judge Timothy J. Kelly (D.D.C.) — Discovery and settlement
docs.x: Judge Timothy J. Kelly, D.D.C.. Discovery and settlement: Comply with LCvR 26.2 and confer in good faith first. No discovery motion without leave; if unresolved, counsel contact chambers jointly to arrange a telephone conference. ADR (mediation, neutral evaluation, or a magistrate judge settlement conference) is available any time by contacting chambers. Promptly advise the court of any full or partial settlement.

docs.t: Judge Eric F. Melgren (D. Kan.) — Oral argument (trap)
docs.x: Judge Eric F. Melgren, D. Kan.. Oral argument (trap): Motions are decided on the papers unless a party affirmatively files a motion seeking oral argument, showing why argument would help the court resolve the issues. A request for argument is no excuse for less than full written briefing. The court may set oral argument on its own; parties are welcome and encouraged to attend.

docs.t: Judge Eric F. Melgren (D. Kan.) — Sealing (trap)
docs.x: Judge Eric F. Melgren, D. Kan.. Sealing (trap): Documents are not automatically sealed because they were produced under a protective order or because the parties stipulate. Before attaching protected documents, first ask the opposing party whether a redaction agreement can avoid sealing. Otherwise, file a motion for leave to file under seal with the proposed sealed documents attached. Both the motion and the response (often the non-movant claims confidentiality) must show good cause with specific facts of public or private harm, not conclusory statements (citing JetAway Aviation and Helm v. Kansas). The court may rule on the papers or set a telephonic hearing. File under seal only after leave is granted; if denied, the court may permit filing not under seal.

docs.t: Judge Eric F. Melgren (D. Kan.) — Filing and brief format
docs.x: Judge Eric F. Melgren, D. Kan.. Filing and brief format: All motions must be filed through ECF; never file a motion during a trial or hearing, or by fax or letter, to get around ECF. No paper copies to chambers unless notified, though counsel may provide them for unusually voluminous or cumbersome filings. Preferred format: proportionally spaced font, 12-point double-spaced text, 10-point single-spaced footnotes; other formats will not be rejected. Statements of fact must cite the record, with copies attached if not already on file, and numerous exhibits should come with an exhibit list.

docs.t: Judge Eric F. Melgren (D. Kan.) — Late filings (trap)
docs.x: Judge Eric F. Melgren, D. Kan.. Late filings (trap): A pleading filed outside the Local Rules’ deadlines must come with a motion for leave to file out of time, with the proposed pleading attached. If leave is granted, the pleading is not filed automatically: the party must then file it, and response times run from that filing.

docs.t: Judge Eric F. Melgren (D. Kan.) — Rulings and chambers contact
docs.x: Judge Eric F. Melgren, D. Kan.. Rulings and chambers contact: Motions are decided in filing order among similar motions, with discovery and non-dispositive motions prioritized over dispositive ones. If a ripe motion seems overlooked, counsel may contact Courtroom Deputy Cindy McKee to confirm it is in the queue. Staff will not predict ruling dates, and the merits may not be discussed.

docs.x: Judge Eric F. Melgren, D. Kan.. Stock jury instructions: The judge posts template civil and criminal jury instructions dated August 2023. The civil set includes preliminary instructions given before the evidence (including note taking and demonstrative exhibits) and a proximate-cause instruction labeled a special instruction not in PIK. The criminal set is keyed to numbered pattern instructions and includes common-offense instructions (aiding and abetting, conspiracy, drug and firearm offenses, false statements, bank fraud) and sample verdict forms, including special drug-quantity findings.

docs.t: Judge John Lungstrum (D. Kan.) — Exhibit marking (trap)
docs.x: Judge John Lungstrum, D. Kan.. Exhibit marking (trap): Exhibits are marked by the courtroom deputy at least 5 days before trial or, with the deputy’s prior approval, by counsel. The instructions name Sharon Scheurer at (913) 551-6579; the page lists chambers at 913-735-2320 and ksd_lungstrum_chambers@ksd.uscourts.gov.

docs.t: Judge John Lungstrum (D. Kan.) — Exhibit numbering (trap)
docs.x: Judge John Lungstrum, D. Kan.. Exhibit numbering (trap): Nos. 1–400 for plaintiffs, 401–800 for defendants, and 801 and higher for any third party. If you expect to exceed your block, contact the courtroom deputy before proceeding. This differs from the court’s newer JERS instructions, which say defendants typically begin at 801; confirm with chambers. Counsel may use their own stickers if they show “Plaintiff’s Exhibit” or “Defendant’s Exhibit,” the exhibit number, and the case number. Giving the deputy an approximate exhibit count lets stickers be prepared in advance.

docs.t: Judge John Lungstrum (D. Kan.) — Exhibit lists and exchange
docs.x: Judge John Lungstrum, D. Kan.. Exhibit lists and exchange: Prepare the District of Kansas exhibit sheet form (or a duplicate containing all its information) before the marking session, even in rough draft. Exchange copies of exhibits 5 days before trial, and bring 3 copies of the exhibit list on the day of trial.

docs.t: Judge John Lungstrum (D. Kan.) — Judge’s copies at trial
docs.x: Judge John Lungstrum, D. Kan.. Judge’s copies at trial: Have a copy of every exhibit for the judge, plus an extra copy for the clerk in a bench trial. Hand the judge’s copy up when the exhibit is offered to the witness for identification; an exhibit notebook for the judge is optional. Provide numbered indexing tabs or file folders for both the original exhibits and the court’s copies.

docs.t: Judge John Lungstrum (D. Kan.) — Depositions and interrogatories
docs.x: Judge John Lungstrum, D. Kan.. Depositions and interrogatories: Original depositions and interrogatory answers are filed in open court as offered. Counsel must provide the original deposition for any testimony read into evidence.

docs.t: Judge John Lungstrum (D. Kan.) — Courtroom equipment
docs.x: Judge John Lungstrum, D. Kan.. Courtroom equipment: The courtroom has a Sony presentation stand (ELMO) that displays paper or laptop documents on monitors at the bench, counsel tables, witness stand, jury box, and deputy and reporter stations. docs.t: Judge John Lungstrum (D. Kan.) — Electronic exhibits for deliberations
docs.x: Judge John Lungstrum, D. Kan.. Electronic exhibits for deliberations: The court’s standard Jury Evidence Recording System (JERS) instructions (revised 9/7/2018), posted on every District of Kansas judge’s page, call for electronic exhibits on a labeled storage device no later than 1 week before trial, named “-_” (letters only in the part field, e.g., 2-a), in .pdf, .jpg, .bmp, .tif, or .gif (or listed audio/video formats), with files no larger than 500MB; misnamed exhibits are returned for reformatting.

docs.t: Judge John W. Broomes (D. Kan.) — Sentencing memoranda (trap)
docs.x: Judge John W. Broomes, D. Kan.. Sentencing memoranda (trap): In all criminal cases assigned to Judge Broomes, sentencing memoranda are optional, but any memorandum must be filed on CM/ECF no later than 5 days before sentencing. A memorandum filed in violation of the standing order may be stricken without further notice.

docs.t: Judge John W. Broomes (D. Kan.) — Jury trial exhibits (JERS)
docs.x: Judge John W. Broomes, D. Kan.. Jury trial exhibits (JERS): The page also posts the court’s standard Jury Evidence Recording System (JERS) instructions (revised 9/7/2018), which appear on most judges’ pages: JERS is used in every jury trial unless the court directs otherwise; exhibits go to chambers on a labeled flash drive, DVD, or CD no later than 1 week before trial, named “-_” (part in letters only, e.g., 2-a), with defense exhibits starting at 801; mislabeled devices are returned for reformatting. Only admitted exhibits are released to the jury, after counsel and the courtroom deputy or law clerk confirm them before deliberations; mark sealed exhibits “SEALED” and note redacted personal identifiers in the description.

docs.t: Judge John W. Broomes (D. Kan.) — Chambers
docs.x: Judge John W. Broomes, D. Kan.. Chambers: Chambers email is ksd_broomes_chambers@ksd.uscourts.gov; Courtroom 238, Wichita.

docs.t: Judge Julie A. Robinson (D. Kan.) — Contacting chambers
docs.x: Judge Julie A. Robinson, D. Kan.. Contacting chambers: Never contact chambers to seek relief; file a motion. For other purposes, email ksd_robinson_chambers@ksd.uscourts.gov with all counsel copied (except where ex parte contact is permitted by law). Avoid phone calls except in emergencies.

docs.t: Judge Julie A. Robinson (D. Kan.) — Page limits (trap)
docs.x: Judge Julie A. Robinson, D. Kan.. Page limits (trap): D. Kan. Rule 7.1(d) (as amended December 1, 2022) governs, but in Judge Robinson’s cases the limit applies to the entire brief except the table of contents, table of authorities, and certificate of service. Do not call chambers with page-limit questions; follow the local rules as supplemented for timing and leave to exceed.

docs.t: Judge Julie A. Robinson (D. Kan.) — TROs and preliminary injunctions (trap)
docs.x: Judge Julie A. Robinson, D. Kan.. TROs and preliminary injunctions (trap): D. Kan. Rule 65.1 governs TROs. A motion seeking a TRO or, alternatively, a preliminary injunction is treated as a preliminary injunction motion unless the movant complies with Fed. R. Civ. P. 65(b). To get a hearing, the movant emails chambers, copying opposing counsel if an appearance has been entered.

docs.x: Judge Julie A. Robinson, D. Kan.. Pretrial conference: In civil cases, the judge holds a pretrial conference after denial of a dispositive motion, when the case is ripe for trial, and sets deadlines tailored to the case.

docs.t: Judge Julie A. Robinson (D. Kan.) — Exhibits (trap)
docs.x: Judge Julie A. Robinson, D. Kan.. Exhibits (trap): Original exhibits must, to the extent possible, be offered in electronic format for jury trials (JERS is used for jury trials, not bench trials). Provide an electronic exhibit list, in the JERS format (confer with Ms. Spegal), with the electronic files at least one week before trial. Civil: to mark exhibits with the courtroom deputy, the parties must jointly request it at least 14 calendar days before trial by emailing chambers. Criminal: all exhibits must be marked and exchanged at least 7 calendar days before the first day of the firm trial setting. Numbering: Nos. 1–800 for plaintiffs (or the United States) and 801 and higher for defendants. Counsel make their own stickers showing “Plaintiff (Name)’s,” “Defendant (Name)’s,” “Government’s,” or “Joint Exhibit,” the number, and the case number. Provide one paper copy of all exhibits for

docs.t: Judge Julie A. Robinson (D. Kan.) — Witness and exhibit lists
docs.x: Judge Julie A. Robinson, D. Kan.. Witness and exhibit lists: Final lists must be limited to witnesses you intend to call and exhibits you intend to use, not everyone with knowledge or everything produced. Good-faith omissions of a previously disclosed item that later becomes important will not be penalized. The parties must confer on exhibits to be admitted without objection, be ready to offer them on day one, and email one list of agreed exhibits in Word to chambers on the first day of trial.

docs.t: Judge Julie A. Robinson (D. Kan.) — Jury instructions (trap)
docs.x: Judge Julie A. Robinson, D. Kan.. Jury instructions (trap): Under D. Kan. R. 51.1 the parties must jointly submit one agreed set of case-specific instructions by the court’s deadline. For disputed instructions, each party submits its own with an explanation and authority of no more than one page. Cite authority for the instruction itself, and avoid case-law language. Don’t propose instructions covered by the judge’s posted stock civil or criminal instructions; those contain no claim- or offense-specific instructions, which the parties must propose. In criminal cases the deadline is set in the Trial Order. To be timely, instructions must both be e-filed and emailed in Word to chambers by the deadline. Objections not raised in the filings or at the informal conference with the law clerk before the close of evidence will not be heard at the formal instruction conference. The court instructs

docs.t: Judge Julie A. Robinson (D. Kan.) — Jury selection and time limits
docs.x: Judge Julie A. Robinson, D. Kan.. Jury selection and time limits: Struck method. Civil: 14 in the box, 3 peremptories per side, usually a jury of 8. Criminal: 32 in the box, 6 peremptories for the government and 10 total for defendants, plus 1 each for alternates; usually 12 jurors and 2 alternates. Peremptories are exercised in writing, alternating, starting with plaintiff or the government. The juror list (name, town, occupation) is available one week before trial. In civil cases, submit a joint statement of the case, generally no more than one page, for the court to read in voir dire. The court conducts extensive voir dire; each party gets 30 total minutes of supplemental questioning and may not argue or indoctrinate. Openings are usually limited to 20 minutes per party and closings to 30 minutes.

docs.t: Judge Julie A. Robinson (D. Kan.) — Trial day and witnesses (trap)
docs.x: Judge Julie A. Robinson, D. Kan.. Trial day and witnesses (trap): Trial hours vary: 9 a.m. to 5 p.m., 8:30 a.m. to 1:30 p.m. with no lunch break, or a combination. Matters outside the jury’s presence go at 8:30 a.m., at breaks, or after the trial day, with advance notice; bench conferences are kept to a minimum. Disclose the next day’s witnesses and exhibits to opposing counsel by 6:00 p.m. the day before. Have enough witnesses for a full day; there should be no dead time. Objections: “objection” plus the basis only (e.g., “hearsay”), no narrative. Give the court reporter your business card and, for technical terms, a glossary before trial.

docs.t: Judge Julie A. Robinson (D. Kan.) — Courtroom conduct
docs.x: Judge Julie A. Robinson, D. Kan.. Courtroom conduct: Stand when addressing the court and when the jury or the court enters or exits. Ask permission to approach the bench (no permission needed to approach a witness). Only one attorney per party examines a witness (Local Rule 43.1(b)), from the lectern, without greeting witnesses or using first names. No commenting on rulings, testimony, or opposing counsel, and no arguing after a ruling. No food, soft drinks, cups with logos, or straws; no boxes or briefcases on counsel tables. If the rule on witnesses is invoked, counsel must instruct their witnesses on the four listed sequestration limits. Avoid any contact with jurors; post-trial juror interviews require a court order (D. Kan. Rule 47.1).

docs.t: Judge Kathryn H. Vratil (D. Kan.) — Trial day and witness disclosure (trap)
docs.x: Judge Kathryn H. Vratil, D. Kan.. Trial day and witness disclosure (trap): The goal is at least 7 hours of uninterrupted testimony every trial day, with legal issues heard outside the jury’s time rather than at bench conferences. Witnesses and exhibits expected to be used must be disclosed to opposing counsel 24 hours in advance, so issues can be raised the next day before the jury is seated or during a recess. On the first day of trial counsel must be present at 8:30 a.m. to go over procedures with the courtroom deputy or law clerk.

docs.t: Judge Kathryn H. Vratil (D. Kan.) — Exhibits and JERS (trap)
docs.x: Judge Kathryn H. Vratil, D. Kan.. Exhibits and JERS (trap): For jury trials, original exhibits must be offered in electronic format to the extent possible, for use in JERS (not used in bench trials). The court’s standard JERS instructions require the exhibit device no later than 1 week before trial, files named “-_” (part in letters only), and defense exhibits starting at 801. At the outset of any hearing or trial, give the court a marked paper copy of exhibits in a 3-ring binder, and tell the courtroom deputy about stipulated exhibits so they can be received at the start. A second paper copy for the witness stand is recommended if you display exhibits electronically. Counsel maintain the official exhibit list, keep a record of exhibits admitted each day, and must review admitted exhibits with the courtroom deputy or law clerk at the end of each trial day.

docs.t: Judge Kathryn H. Vratil (D. Kan.) — Civil jury selection (trap)
docs.x: Judge Kathryn H. Vratil, D. Kan.. Civil jury selection (trap): The court seats 8 to 10 jurors in a civil jury trial; each side has 3 peremptory challenges. The court conducts initial voir dire on standard subjects (biography, knowledge of the case, counsel, or witnesses, prior jury service and litigation, experience with the subject matter, hardship), so counsel need not propose questions on them. Each party then gets 20 minutes of supplemental questioning. In voir dire counsel may not argue, seek promises, ask about the law, jury instructions, or opinions on hypothetical facts, or otherwise try to ingratiate or indoctrinate the jury.

docs.t: Judge Kathryn H. Vratil (D. Kan.) — Openings, closings, and jurors
docs.x: Judge Kathryn H. Vratil, D. Kan.. Openings, closings, and jurors: Absent prior leave, each party gets 20 minutes for opening statement and 20 minutes for closing argument. Jurors may take notes, and the court may allow juror questions, screened before being asked in open court.

docs.t: Judge Kathryn H. Vratil (D. Kan.) — Courtroom etiquette
docs.x: Judge Kathryn H. Vratil, D. Kan.. Courtroom etiquette: Stand when court opens, recesses, and adjourns, when the jury enters or leaves, and when addressing or addressed by the court (counsel with physical disabilities excused). Refer to everyone, including witnesses, by surname with Mr., Ms., or another title, never by first name or nickname.

docs.t: Judge Kathryn H. Vratil (D. Kan.) — Courtroom technology and court reporting
docs.x: Judge Kathryn H. Vratil, D. Kan.. Courtroom technology and court reporting: Monitors at bench, witness stand, counsel tables, and jury box, an ELMO document camera, and HDMI ports at counsel tables; whiteboards, screens, and easels as available. Arrange training or ask questions through Courtroom Deputy Jeff Hokanson, 913-735-2207. Give the court reporter a list of correctly spelled unusual or technical names and terms your witnesses will use.

docs.t: Judge Kathryn H. Vratil (D. Kan.) — Criminal: Speedy Trial continuances (trap)
docs.x: Judge Kathryn H. Vratil, D. Kan.. Criminal: Speedy Trial continuances (trap): Under Pretrial Order No. 1, a motion to extend the 70-day trial deadline and exclude time under 18 U.S.C. § 3161(h)(7) must be filed jointly by the deadline set (at least 7 days before the status conference), with any disagreement set out in the joint motion. Later extension motions are closely scrutinized. Conclusory or boilerplate motions tracking the statute are insufficient (citing United States v. Toombs). The motion must address the listed factors (why the event requires time, complexity, diligence, other trials, witness unavailability, the defendant’s position, multi-defendant dates) and propose a firm schedule for discovery, motions, hearings, and trial days. Press of other business is ordinarily not enough; such a motion must address whether other counsel in the office could try the case. Counsel must

docs.t: Judge Kathryn H. Vratil (D. Kan.) — Criminal discovery
docs.x: Judge Kathryn H. Vratil, D. Kan.. Criminal discovery: Pretrial Order No. 1 makes discovery obligations self-executing; no request is needed, and boilerplate discovery motions are discouraged. The government’s Rule 16 disclosures are due at least 14 days before the pretrial-motion deadline, and the defendant’s reciprocal, alibi, and insanity disclosures within 14 days after. Brady material and Rule 404(b) notice (stating the specific purpose) are due no later than 14 days before trial; Giglio material sufficiently in advance for effective use. The court strongly urges Jencks statements at least 48 hours before the witness testifies. Expert summaries are due only on written request. Additional discovery requires a motion with memorandum and authority. Deadlines run from the original arraignment and do not restart on superseding charges; request a status conference if changes are needed.

docs.t: Judge Kathryn H. Vratil (D. Kan.) — Criminal pretrial and trial
docs.x: Judge Kathryn H. Vratil, D. Kan.. Criminal pretrial and trial: Under Pretrial Order No. 2, at least 14 days before the final pretrial conference counsel must finish conferring to narrow issues and file stipulations of fact and law, final witness and exhibit lists, and motions in limine; responses are due at least 7 days before the conference, where motions in limine are argued. Trial settings are firm; continuances only for truly extraordinary circumstances. Tell the courtroom deputy immediately of a plea change or if fewer trial days are needed. Special voir dire requests and proposed jury instructions are due at least 7 days before trial; do not propose routine, standard instructions.

docs.t: Judge Kathryn H. Vratil (D. Kan.) — Stock jury instructions
docs.x: Judge Kathryn H. Vratil, D. Kan.. Stock jury instructions: The judge posts stock civil jury instructions (general instructions on evidence, credibility, experts, preponderance, intent, proximate cause, and a unanimous verdict on verdict-form questions), with a disclaimer that they may change without notice and counsel should watch for intervening changes in local rules or case law.

docs.t: Judge Toby Crouse (D. Kan.) — Stock civil jury instructions
docs.x: Judge Toby Crouse, D. Kan.. Stock civil jury instructions: The judge posts a full template of civil jury instructions (preliminary and final instructions plus a verdict form), available in PDF and Word. Claim-specific instructions on elements, standards, damages, and definitions are “to be proposed by parties, with appropriate citations.” Bracketed optional instructions cover stipulations, judicial notice, expert testimony, deposition testimony, limited-purpose evidence, redacted exhibits, a clear-and-convincing standard (e.g., fiduciary relationship or fraud under state law), and alternate jurors.

docs.t: Judge Toby Crouse (D. Kan.) — Preliminary instruction and openings (trap)
docs.x: Judge Toby Crouse, D. Kan.. Preliminary instruction and openings (trap): The preliminary instruction summarizes each side’s claims and defenses using a description “either jointly submitted or provided to the parties with opportunity to object on the record.” The template gives each side 20 minutes for opening statements.

docs.t: Judge Toby Crouse (D. Kan.) — Instructions before closings (trap)

Instead of the written discovery plan under L.R. 16.1(a)(2), file the joint case management plan on the posted form and email a Word copy to chambers. Trial should be within 9 months of the conference absent unusual circumstances. Bring calendars (tell the CSO if you need to bring an internet-capable device to the conference room). If you want trial outside Cheyenne (such as Casper or Jackson), confer and raise it at the conference. Stipulated extensions of filing deadlines need court approval; the schedule changes only for good cause, and the final pretrial conference and trial dates are held firm barring unforeseen circumstances.

docs.x: Judge Nancy D. Freudenthal, D. Wyo.. A defendant must give 30 days’ notice before contacting or subpoenaing the plaintiff’s current or prospective employer. Do not file discovery notices in CM/ECF, but do file all expert designations and reports, including supplements. Experts are limited to one per field per side absent complex issues; treating providers must be designated as experts. Expert depositions may follow the fact cutoff but must finish 14 days before the final pretrial conference. Ch

Email (don’t file) the joint proposed final pretrial order in Word, on the posted form, 7 days before the conference; plaintiff takes the lead and separate submissions are not permitted. Counsel appear in person in chambers. Exhibit objections are coded Category A, B, or C; unlisted exhibits may be excluded and unstated objections deemed waived. Authentication requests are due in writing within 5 business days after an exhibit is made available. Deposition designations go out 10 business days before trial, objections 5 business days, and unresolved disputes to the court 3 business days before trial. Motions in limine: one motion per side covering all issues, filed 14 days before the final pretrial conference after conferring, with respo

docs.t: Judge Nancy D. Freudenthal (D. Wyo.) — Jury trial filings and selection
docs.x: Judge Nancy D. Freudenthal, D. Wyo.. Jury trial filings and selection: File (PDF) and email (Word) proposed voir dire, joint jury instructions, and a joint special verdict form 7 days before trial. Plaintiff leads drafting; submit only substantive instructions with citations, as a single Word document in reading order, split into agreed, plaintiff’s disputed, and defendant’s disputed sets if needed, plus a joint noncontentious statement of the case. Fourteen jurors are seated for voir dire; each side gets 3 peremptories and 8 jurors try the case, with no alternates. Attorney voir dire is typically 15 minutes; don’t argue the case or seek commitments, and say “pass for cause” rather than raising cause challenges before the jury. No separate juror questionnaire absent extraordinary circumstances. Counsel usually get the venire list the Wednesday before trial; contacting prospective jurors

docs.t: Judge Nancy D. Freudenthal (D. Wyo.) — Trial logistics
docs.x: Judge Nancy D. Freudenthal, D. Wyo.. Trial logistics: On the first day of a jury trial, report to chambers at 8:30 a.m. Trial days run 8:30 to 5:00. Openings are typically 30 minutes per side. Electronic exhibits go to the Clerk’s Office for JERS by 8:30 a.m. 5 days before trial (files up to 500MB each). No paper exhibit copies are needed; originals go to the deputy clerk as admitted. Send the court reporter a witness list 5 business days before trial (the Pointers say at least one week, with keyword indices); request real-time or daily copy 14 days ahead. To reserve an attorney room or test technology, contact the courtroom deputy at least 2 weeks before trial. Each morning, give the other side, the deputy, and the reporter a list of exhibits for each witness, or risk a fine.

docs.t: Judge Nancy D. Freudenthal (D. Wyo.) — Courtroom conduct (trap)
docs.x: Judge Nancy D. Freudenthal, D. Wyo.. Courtroom conduct (trap): Stand to object and state the specific rule (for example, “irrelevant and inadmissible under Rule 402”); no speaking objections. Stay at the main podium unless permitted to approach; lavaliere microphones need permission. Mute counsel-table microphones during private conversations because jurors’ hearing devices pick them up. Only one attorney per party examines each witness, and the attorney who objects on direct handles cross and sidebar. Don’t greet witnesses or use first names. Expert reports are not admitted, nor are attorney-prepared charts of testimony unless the witness endorses them. Never make Golden Rule or “reptile” arguments, personal opinions, or appeals to a party’s wealth or ability to pay. During deliberations, be able to return within about 15 minutes and give the deputy two phone numbers.

docs.t: Judge Nancy D. Freudenthal (D. Wyo.) — Bench trials
docs.x: Judge Nancy D. Freudenthal, D. Wyo.. Bench trials: Each side files proposed findings and conclusions 5 business days before trial, emailed in Word, following the judge’s guidelines: numbered simple declarative sentences based on expected evidence, without testimony recitals, pejoratives, or legal conclusions, plus numbered legal conclusions with authority. Witness statements for experts and technical witnesses without significant credibility issues are exchanged and filed 7 days before the final pretrial conference. They are required for parties and witnesses under their control, but not for adverse parties or subpoenaed witnesses. The witness adopts the statement under oath, then may supplement live before cross.

docs.t: Judge Nancy D. Freudenthal (D. Wyo.) — Settlement and ADR
docs.x: Judge Nancy D. Freudenthal, D. Wyo.. Settlement and ADR: Consider mediation or a settlement conference well before the pre-dispositive-motion status conference. For court-assisted settlement, contact either of the District’s full-time magistrate judges.

Parties may ask in their papers to submit without argument; the court may take any motion under submission (L.R. 230(g)) and will say so by minute order before the hearing.

docs.x: Judge Dale A. Drozd, E.D. Cal.. TROs, ex parte, and administrative relief: TROs and injunctions follow FRCP 65 and L.R. 231. The court typically won’t rule until at least 24 hours after the opposing party is served, and that party may file papers in the meantime. Ex parte applications are usually decided on the papers. Before filing, contact the courtroom deputy and the opposing party; state whether an opposition will be filed; and attach an affidavit explaining the need for the order, why a stipulation couldn’t be obtained, and why the matter can’t be noticed under L.R. 230. Administrative matters (page extensions, shortened time, briefing or non-dispositive discovery schedule changes) go by L.R. 233 motion with a proposed order.

Only the proponent of sealing may ask, so a party filing material the other side has marked confidential must give enough advance notice for that side to seek sealing. E-file the Notice of Request to Seal; email the request, a proposed sealing order in Word, and the documents to dadorders@caed.uscourts.gov. Once the order issues, email the documents to ApprovedSealed@caed.uscourts.gov for filing under seal.

docs.x: Judge Dale A. Drozd, E.D. Cal.. Separate statements are allowed only for unrepresented parties. The statement must include a neutral joint statement of the case; list overlapping exhibits as joint exhibits (JX-1, JX-2); number plaintiff’s exhibits and letter defendant’s; describe each exhibit in detail (date, Bates number, description, page length); state every remaining issue under points of law or mark it abandoned; and list only motions in limine reasonably expected. Do not file motions in limine before the pretrial conference; the pretrial order sets those dates, exhibit submission, and other trial deadlines.

docs.x: Judge Dena M. Coggins, E.D. Cal.. Sentencing and supervised release: PSR objections go to probation and the other side at least 28 days before sentencing; formal objections, including to special conditions, are filed at least 14 days before. Requests to continue sentencing must come from the requesting party and state reasons with particularity. Motions for early termination of supervised release must state the positions of Probation, the defendant, and the government; if granted, the defendant files a probation-approved proposed order within 5 days.

docs.t: Judge Kirk E. Sherriff (E.D. Cal.) — Trial

Plaintiff (or the removing defendant) must serve the standing order on all parties, and parties should check the judge’s web page for changes before acting in a case.

docs.t: Judge Troy Nunley (E.D. Cal.) — Civil motions and page limits (trap)
docs.x: Judge Troy Nunley, E.D. Cal.. Civil motions and page limits (trap): Memoranda supporting or opposing a motion are capped at 20 pages and replies at 10. Times New Roman no smaller than 12 point (Courier no smaller than 10); footnotes no more than one size smaller, used sparingly. Paginate multi-page exhibits internally from 1 and cite as “Ex. A at 7.” Searchable (OCR or hyperlinked) filings are encouraged. Cite cases to the specific page, preferring Westlaw over Lexis for unpublished cases; list the more authoritative source first; and cite statutes to the specific section and subsection (no “et seq.”).

docs.t: Judge Troy Nunley (E.D. Cal.) — Meet and confer and waiver (trap)
docs.x: Judge Troy Nunley, E.D. Cal.. Meet and confer and waiver (trap): In counseled cases, meet and confer thoroughly before filing any motion, including summary judgment. Plaintiff’s counsel should weigh the claimed pleading defects and often agree to an amendment that would cure a curable defect. All purely legal issues must be raised by timely pretrial motion; failing to raise a dispositive legal issue before the dispositive-motion cut-off may waive it.

docs.t: Judge Troy Nunley (E.D. Cal.) — Courtesy copies, proposed orders, and contact
docs.x: Judge Troy Nunley, E.D. Cal.. Courtesy copies, proposed orders, and contact: No paper courtesy copies of pleadings or exhibits unless ordered. Email every proposed order in Word to tlnorders@caed.uscourts.gov in addition to e-filing the PDF, with the case number and “proposed order” in the subject line (L.R. 137(b)). Do not contact the judge or chambers staff by phone, email, or other ex parte means; appropriate inquiries go to the courtroom deputy. Promptly notify the court whenever a case may be transferred by the JPML, whether or not you are a party to the JPML filing.

docs.t: Judge Troy Nunley (E.D. Cal.) — Ex parte, TROs, and extensions (trap)
docs.x: Judge Troy Nunley, E.D. Cal.. Ex parte, TROs, and extensions (trap): Use L.R. 233 for administrative relief; an ex parte application is for relief unavailable that way and is usually decided on the papers. Oppositions are due within 48 hours (72 hours if the application is filed on a Friday). For TROs and injunctions, the court typically won’t rule until at least 24 hours after the opposing party is served. Stipulations extending schedule dates are not effective until approved; agreement alone is not good cause, and witness or counsel unavailability rarely is. Designate experts with signed Rule 26(a)(2)(B) reports per the Initial Pretrial Scheduling Order, identifying each as percipient, retained, or both. A late designator’s supplemental list is limited to rebuttal, and undesignated experts testify only on the good-cause showing the order describes. A settlement conference may be set at the final pretrial conference or earlier on joint written request, before a randomly assigned magistrate judge or through VDRP. docs.x: Judge Bernard A. Friedman, E.D. Mich.. docs.x: Judge Bernard A. Friedman, E.D. Mich.. docs.x: Judge Bernard A. Friedman, E.D. Mich.. Jury selection and courtroom conduct: Striking method; the court conducts preliminary voir dire and allows reasonable voir dire by counsel, and challenges are handled so jurors do not know who excused them. In criminal cases two alternates are normally used and are not told they are alternates until the end. Only one lawyer per party may examine a given witness. Ask permission to approach the witness or bench; stand to speak, but you need not stay at the podium and may approach the jury box. Time limits on openings and closings are possible. The jury is charged before closing arguments and is given a copy of the instructions. Jurors typically may not take notes unless both sides agree.

docs.x: Judge Bernard A. Friedman, E.D. Mich.. docs.x: Judge Bernard A. Friedman, E.D. Mich.. Pleas and sentencing: The court accepts Alford and nolo contendere pleas, sometimes over government objection, and will accept a plea agreement capping the sentence at a stated period above the bottom of the guideline range. Guideline disputes are typically resolved at sentencing, and a rejected Rule 11 agreement is announced in open court. Self-reporting may be allowed.
