docs.t: Judge David M. Lawson (E.D. Mich.) — Sealing and protective orders (trap)
docs.x: Judge David M. Lawson, E.D. Mich.. Sealing and protective orders (trap): File a motion for leave (after seeking concurrence) before docketing anything under seal. If the motion is not itself sensitive, e-file it publicly with the items as separately docketed sealed exhibits; if it is sensitive or must be kept from opposing counsel, send everything as separate Word files through CM/ECF Utilities to the case manager and e-file nothing. Requests to seal whole briefs or all exhibits for limited sensitive content are usually denied. Agreed protective orders are encouraged: e-file a stipulation and send the proposed order through Utilities. The stipulation must include the judge’s required “Filing Under Seal” language (no advance sealing authority; motion under L.R. 5.3 and Shane Group) and a provision requiring notice to the designating party before filing its confidential material.

docs.t: Judge David M. Lawson (E.D. Mich.) — Stipulations, contact, and settlement notice
docs.x: Judge David M. Lawson, E.D. Mich.. Stipulations, contact, and settlement notice: E-file stipulations; send the proposed order separately through CM/ECF Utilities in Word. Combined stipulation-orders are discouraged. A non-e-filing pro se party must sign in ink. No ex parte communications. Contact the case manager or judicial assistant only on procedural and scheduling matters; contacting law clerks is discouraged. Report a settlement in writing by email or fax by the next business day.

docs.t: Judge David M. Lawson (E.D. Mich.) — Scheduling and discovery
docs.x: Judge David M. Lawson, E.D. Mich.. Scheduling and discovery: Counsel, preferably lead counsel, must attend the case management conference in person. Before it, email chambers (do not e-file) a short double-spaced statement of the case, or docket a joint Rule 26(f) statement covering the notice’s items; discuss ADR with clients beforehand. Rule 26(a)(1) disclosures are generally due 14 days after the conference. An expert’s identity must be disclosed within 3 business days of retention. Discovery may be extended by stipulation only if motion, final pretrial, and trial dates are unaffected; other extensions are not routinely granted and need good cause by stipulation or by a motion stating concurrence was sought and refused. Before a discovery motion, the parties are encouraged to email a joint letter and schedule a phone conference. Discovery motions are generally referred to the magistra

docs.t: Judge David M. Lawson (E.D. Mich.) — Removal and TROs
docs.x: Judge David M. Lawson, E.D. Mich.. Removal and TROs: Many removed cases get a standing order requiring the removing party, within 7 days, to explain any missing joinder, timeliness, forum-defendant issues, full citizenship of all parties (including members of non-corporate entities), the amount in controversy, or the federal basis. Plaintiff may respond within 14 court days. Remand motions for procedural defects are due within 30 days of removal. TROs without notice are rarely granted absent a true emergency where notice would cause the harm. Call the case manager on filing an injunction motion.

docs.t: Judge David M. Lawson (E.D. Mich.) — Final pretrial (trap)
docs.x: Judge David M. Lawson, E.D. Mich.. Final pretrial (trap): Final pretrial and settlement conference about 2 weeks before trial. The joint final pretrial order follows the scheduling order’s format (which may supersede parts of L.R. 16.2) and is submitted to chambers, not e-filed, at least 1 week before the conference. Trial counsel, natural-person parties, a representative of other parties, and any controlling insurer must attend in person with “full authority,” meaning authority exceeding plaintiff’s last demand; phone availability does not count, and Rule 16(f) sanctions apply. Motions in limine are generally due 5 weeks before the final pretrial conference. Requests for equipment, interpreters, accommodations, and daily or real-time transcripts must be made at or before the conference. Case evaluation requires a stipulation to be bound by Mich. Ct. R. 2.403, including sanctions; facili

docs.t: Judge David M. Lawson (E.D. Mich.) — Trial submissions
docs.x: Judge David M. Lawson, E.D. Mich.. Trial submissions: At least 1 week before trial: stipulated jury instructions (no boilerplate; the court’s standard instructions are available from the case manager) with Word-compatible media certified virus free, separately filed disputed instructions, voir dire requests, a statement of claims or defenses of no more than 2 pages, witness and exhibit lists on the court’s form, and optional trial briefs (mandatory in bench trials). Bench trials: proposed findings and conclusions at least 1 week before trial, one fact per paragraph with exhibit or testimony citations, plus a Word copy.

docs.t: Judge David M. Lawson (E.D. Mich.) — Trial (trap)
docs.x: Judge David M. Lawson, E.D. Mich.. Trial (trap): Trials run Monday through Friday; jury trials generally begin Tuesday. After day one, trial usually runs 8 a.m. to about 2 p.m. with two 15-minute breaks (occasionally 8:30–12:30 and 1:45–5). Deliver the exhibit book 1 day before trial. Documents and photos must be published electronically, with two hard-copy sets (court and jury). All counsel and assistants must schedule a joint technology tutorial with the court’s IT staff at least 1 week before trial. Show opening-statement exhibits to opposing counsel in advance. The court conducts initial voir dire and usually allows probative follow-up by counsel; peremptories alternate. Evidentiary stipulations must be in writing, signed by counsel (and the defendant in criminal cases). Purge deposition testimony of objections well before trial. Jurors may take notes but may not question witnesses.

docs.t: Judge David M. Lawson (E.D. Mich.) — Criminal cases
docs.x: Judge David M. Lawson, E.D. Mich.. Criminal cases: A signed Rule 11 plea agreement must reach chambers by the plea cutoff, about 2 weeks before trial; after that, only a plea as charged is accepted. Rule 11(c)(1)(B) and (C) agreements are acceptable. The defendant must attend all hearings and the final pretrial conference, and writs must be submitted 4 weeks ahead. Stand-in counsel at the final pretrial conference is not allowed except in extraordinary circumstances with permission and client consent. Witness lists, voir dire, stipulated instructions, and exhibit lists go directly to chambers, not e-filed, usually 1 week before trial; a defense-theory instruction is due on the first day of trial. Jencks material is strongly encouraged by the day before the final pretrial conference. Sentencing (standing order, January 24, 2024): defense arranges a probation interview within 7 days of con

docs.t: Judge Denise Page Hood (E.D. Mich.) — Courtesy copies (trap)
docs.x: Judge Denise Page Hood, E.D. Mich.. Courtesy copies (trap): Send chambers a courtesy copy of all motions, dispositive and non-dispositive, plus responses, replies, and all exhibits. Bind on the left side (no rubber bands or binder clips), use exhibit labels that extend beyond the side of the paper, and attach a printed Notice of Electronic Filing to the front. Mail it first class the same day you e-file. If the filing relates to a proceeding within the next 5 days or otherwise needs immediate attention, hand-deliver it to chambers by the morning of the next business day. Also provide courtesy copies, with all exhibits, of every complaint over 20 pages and every notice of removal.

docs.t: Judge Denise Page Hood (E.D. Mich.) — Motions and concurrence (trap)
docs.x: Judge Denise Page Hood, E.D. Mich.. Motions and concurrence (trap): L.R. 5.1, L.R. 7.1, and the Electronic Filing Policies and Procedures are strictly enforced for all motions. Concurrence under L.R. 7.1(a) requires a good-faith effort that normally means actual contact with opposing counsel. If no conversation occurs, the motion must specifically describe the reasonable efforts made; the outcome of the conference must be stated, and all of it documented specifically in the motion papers. Hearings are held on most motions, usually on Wednesday afternoons.

docs.t: Judge Denise Page Hood (E.D. Mich.) — Conferences
docs.x: Judge Denise Page Hood, E.D. Mich.. Conferences: A Rule 16(b) scheduling conference is held after the answer is filed; the scheduling order and a standing order on the Joint Final Pretrial Order issue then. Status conferences are set case by case. Conferences are generally held on Monday afternoons. Out-of-state counsel may attend scheduling and status conferences (but not pretrial or settlement conferences) by telephone if arranged in advance. Parties generally must attend pretrial and settlement conferences.

docs.t: Judge Denise Page Hood (E.D. Mich.) — Discovery
docs.x: Judge Denise Page Hood, E.D. Mich.. Discovery: The court usually allows 4–6 months for discovery. The cutoff may be extended by stipulation only if the change does not affect the motion cutoff or final pretrial dates; otherwise, by motion. Discovery motions are generally referred to a magistrate judge.

docs.t: Judge Denise Page Hood (E.D. Mich.) — TROs and injunctions
docs.x: Judge Denise Page Hood, E.D. Mich.. TROs and injunctions: The court follows Fed. R. Civ. P. 65 and grants ex parte relief only in extraordinary circumstances. Briefing is typically accelerated, and hearings are set as the urgency requires.

docs.t: Judge Denise Page Hood (E.D. Mich.) — Removal
docs.x: Judge Denise Page Hood, E.D. Mich.. Removal: If jurisdiction is questionable, the court issues an order to show cause or waits for a motion to remand. It will not dismiss or remand sua sponte without notice to the parties.

docs.t: Judge Denise Page Hood (E.D. Mich.) — Final pretrial and settlement (trap)
docs.x: Judge Denise Page Hood, E.D. Mich.. Final pretrial and settlement (trap): The proposed Joint Final Pretrial Order, signed by counsel for all parties, is due 1 week before the final pretrial conference; under the form scheduling order, compliance with Local Rule 16.2 is mandatory. Trial counsel and the parties, or a representative with full settlement authority, must attend the settlement conference and the final pretrial conference, where settlement is emphasized. The judge routinely takes part in settlement talks in jury cases and refers non-jury cases to another judge or a magistrate judge for a settlement conference. The form order may refer a case to Wayne County Mediation, and no motions other than motions in limine may be filed after the motion cutoff.

docs.t: Judge Denise Page Hood (E.D. Mich.) — Trial
docs.x: Judge Denise Page Hood, E.D. Mich.. Trial: Date-certain docket. The court follows L.R. 16.8 on trial briefs and exhibits; plaintiffs use numbers and defendants use letters. A bench book of exhibits is not required but preferred, especially for bench trials. File motions in limine 1 week before the final pretrial conference. Bench trials: proposed findings and trial briefs are due on the first day of trial. Jury trials: the court conducts voir dire but lets counsel participate for 10–15 minutes per side; objectionable voir dire questions must be submitted in writing before voir dire starts. Jury instructions follow L.R. 16.8(d) and must be filed by the first day of trial. The jury is typically charged after closing arguments and may take available written instructions into the jury room; note-taking is decided case by case. Criminal trials are set under the speedy trial guidelines. The co

docs.t: Judge F. Kay Behm (E.D. Mich.) — Courtesy copies (trap)
docs.x: Judge F. Kay Behm, E.D. Mich.. Courtesy copies (trap): Page: a paper copy of all dispositive motion papers (motions, responses, replies, and exhibits), plus non-dispositive papers whose brief and exhibits exceed 20 pages. Exhibit labels must extend beyond the page edge, papers must be permanently secured on the left (no rubber bands or binder clips), and a printed Notice of Electronic Filing goes on the front. Mail it first class the same day you e-file; if it relates to a proceeding within the next 5 days or needs immediate attention, hand-deliver it by the morning of the next business day. The Phase I case management order template is broader: a courtesy copy of all motions and briefs with exhibits, book-bound on the left, with relevant exhibit portions highlighted. The criminal order requires copies only when brief and exhibits exceed 20 pages.

docs.t: Judge F. Kay Behm (E.D. Mich.) — Motion format and concurrence (trap)
docs.x: Judge F. Kay Behm, E.D. Mich.. Motion format and concurrence (trap): Strict LR 7.1(a) compliance, with costs for failure. The case management order requires the first paragraph of every motion to certify concurrence efforts using one of four prescribed statements (spoke or met and denied; wrote and denied; wrote and 3 business days passed; exceptional circumstances), or the motion is stricken. Briefs in 14-point type, double spaced, Bluebook citations, record cites as “ECF No. 1-2, PageID.1234,” and docket-and-page cites for any opposing argument referenced. If brief and exhibits exceed 12 pages, include a table of contents, table of authorities, and index. No counsel listings or state-court-style matter in captions. Oversized briefs are not routinely allowed; per the case management order, seek extra pages or more time by concise stipulated order (or ex parte motion for pages) filed at

docs.t: Judge F. Kay Behm (E.D. Mich.) — Briefing and hearings
docs.x: Judge F. Kay Behm, E.D. Mich.. Briefing and hearings: No briefing schedule is usually issued; LR 7.1(e) and Rule 6 deadlines apply and are enforced even if the hearing is far off. Counsel who respond late may not argue. Most dispositive motions and most non-dispositive and post-trial motions are heard, except reconsideration and prisoner pro se motions; argument may be cancelled. Bring a proposed order to the hearing. If a pending motion is resolved, email the case manager within 1 business day and the movant must file a notice withdrawing it. If a case settles, notify chambers by email by the next business day.

docs.t: Judge F. Kay Behm (E.D. Mich.) — Summary judgment (trap)
docs.x: Judge F. Kay Behm, E.D. Mich.. Summary judgment (trap): One summary judgment motion per party without leave. The motion must begin with a Statement of Material Facts in numbered paragraphs with pinpoint record cites; it counts against the page limit, and no separate narrative facts section is allowed. Cited sources go in an indexed, tabbed Fact Appendix; chambers copies of appendices over 20 pages must be separately bound with a cover sheet. The response must begin with a Counterstatement using matching numbers; facts not specifically contested are deemed admitted. Skip boilerplate standards and string cites, and submit copies of unpublished or specialty-reporter opinions.

docs.t: Judge F. Kay Behm (E.D. Mich.) — Scheduling and discovery
docs.x: Judge F. Kay Behm, E.D. Mich.. Scheduling and discovery: The scheduling notice issues 2 to 4 weeks after the responsive pleading (after all defendants answer, unless that causes significant delay). File the Rule 26(f) plan or case summary at least 7 days before the conference; lead counsel must attend, and clients should have been advised on ADR. Typical Phase I deadlines: lay witness list, exhibit list, and plaintiff’s expert disclosures 6 weeks before discovery closes; defendant’s experts 2 weeks before; rebuttal reports by the close; facilitator choice to the case manager 1 month before the close; facilitation 30 days after the close; dispositive and expert-exclusion motions 30 days after facilitation. Initial disclosures: 14 days after the conference per the page, but 4 weeks after the scheduling order per the template. Discovery matters are globally referred to the magistrate judge;

docs.t: Judge F. Kay Behm (E.D. Mich.) — TROs, sealing, and orders
docs.x: Judge F. Kay Behm, E.D. Mich.. TROs, sealing, and orders: Every TRO, even ex parte, requires some notice and a chance to hear both sides unless good cause is shown. Email the case manager when filing an injunction motion; a conference is usually held first. Sealing requires a motion under LR 5.3 plus redacted and unredacted versions; a sample motion is posted. In criminal cooperation matters, submit a combined motion and proposed order in Word through CM/ECF Utilities. File a proposed order with every stipulation, submitted in Word through Utilities (not e-filed) and never on letterhead. A pro se non-e-filer must wet-sign the stipulation. No pro hac vice; non-Michigan bar members need local counsel.

docs.t: Judge F. Kay Behm (E.D. Mich.) — Final pretrial and trial (trap)
docs.x: Judge F. Kay Behm, E.D. Mich.. Final pretrial and trial (trap): Phase II template: other motions, including motions in limine, and the joint final pretrial order are due 6 weeks before the final pretrial conference; proposed jury instructions 3 weeks before trial; jury trial on the Tuesday 2 weeks after the conference. Adjournments are rarely granted. Trial counsel, natural-person parties, a representative with full settlement authority, and any controlling insurer must attend the final pretrial conference in person; phone availability does not count without prior permission, generally given only with all counsel’s consent. Foundation and authenticity objections are waived unless noticed at or before the final pretrial conference. Plaintiff uses numbers, defendant letters; make exhibits available for inspection 1 week before the conference; each side keeps custody of its admitted exhibit

docs.t: Judge F. Kay Behm (E.D. Mich.) — Jury instructions and jurors
docs.x: Judge F. Kay Behm, E.D. Mich.. Jury instructions and jurors: Submit a single stipulated set to chambers, double spaced, one instruction per page with authority, on a USB drive in Word; disputed instructions go in separately in the same form and are settled at a hearing on the record. The court gives its own introductory and concluding instructions and charges the jury before closing arguments. Jurors may take notes; juror questions are decided case by case. Arrange courtroom technology, interpreters, and witness accommodations with chambers at least 10 days ahead.

docs.t: Judge F. Kay Behm (E.D. Mich.) — Criminal cases
docs.x: Judge F. Kay Behm, E.D. Mich.. Criminal cases: Counsel meet and confer within 10 days of arraignment, or the government files the 03-AO-027 discovery notice. Motion cutoff is 20 days after arraignment. Schedule changes require a motion with a stipulation and, if trial moves, a Speedy Trial waiver. A writ for a defendant’s presence must be submitted 4 weeks before the court date. Motions in limine and notices contesting foundation, chain of custody, or scientific analysis are due at or before the final pretrial conference, with item-by-item reasons; scientific-analysis contests need notice at least 7 days before trial. Exhibits use yellow government (numbers) and blue defense (letters) stickers, and all witnesses testify in plain clothes. Usually 6 peremptories for the government and 10 for the defense, 12 jurors plus 2 alternates chosen by random draw; Sixth Circuit pattern instructions

docs.t: Judge F. Kay Behm (E.D. Mich.) — Patent cases
docs.x: Judge F. Kay Behm, E.D. Mich.. Patent cases: A Model Rule 26(f) Report and Proposed Scheduling Order applies, setting a typical trial about 20.5 months after the scheduling conference; contentions, claim construction, and expert deadlines run from the scheduling order and claim construction opinion. Be ready to discuss appointing a special master. Claim construction briefs: 25 pages opening, 25 response, 7 reply, in 14-point font; extensions by written motion. An off-the-record technology tutorial precedes the hearing; live testimony requires a written motion and is typically capped at 1 hour per side. Until a protective order is entered, confidential material is produced outside-counsel-eyes-only. Liability and damages trials are normally bifurcated before the same jury.

docs.t: Judge George Caram Steeh III (E.D. Mich.) — Motions and hearings (trap)
docs.x: Judge George Caram Steeh III, E.D. Mich.. Motions and hearings (trap): The court issues the notice of hearing; the movant need not. Oral argument is typically set on all motions except motions to remand and facially frivolous motions. A party that does not respond on time may not argue at the hearing, and response and reply deadlines are enforced even when the hearing is far off. The movant must submit a proposed order (in Word, per the 6/18 order) through CM/ECF Utilities with every motion. Strict compliance with L.R. 7.1 concurrence is required; the patent order says costs will be imposed for noncompliance. Page-limit extensions are obtained by stipulated order or ex parte motion and are granted more often than not. Nondispositive motions, especially discovery motions, are typically referred to the magistrate judge.

docs.t: Judge George Caram Steeh III (E.D. Mich.) — Courtesy copies (trap)
docs.x: Judge George Caram Steeh III, E.D. Mich.. Courtesy copies (trap): Courtesy copies are required. The scheduling order requires a paper copy, labeled “Judge’s Copy,” of electronically filed motions, briefs, attachments, responses, replies, the proposed final pretrial order, and proposed jury instructions, and separately a courtesy copy of all pleadings over 20 pages with exhibits securely fastened. A paper judge’s copy of the final pretrial order goes to chambers immediately after e-filing.

docs.t: Judge George Caram Steeh III (E.D. Mich.) — Summary judgment
docs.x: Judge George Caram Steeh III, E.D. Mich.. Summary judgment: Leave is required for more than one summary judgment motion; a challenge to several counts generally must be in a single motion. Support each fact in the statement of material facts with citations to pleadings, interrogatories, admissions, depositions, affidavits, or documentary exhibits. Skip boilerplate and string cites in favor of a few recent controlling cases, and submit copies of unpublished or specialty-reporter opinions cited.

docs.t: Judge George Caram Steeh III (E.D. Mich.) — Scheduling and discovery
docs.x: Judge George Caram Steeh III, E.D. Mich.. Scheduling and discovery: The court sets a scheduling conference after the answer (usually after all defendants answer, and after a ruling if a dispositive motion is filed instead). A Rule 26(f) plan is due one week before the conference; come ready to discuss jurisdiction, case evaluation or facilitation, and scheduling. The court expects the parties to agree to some form of ADR and to follow the district’s model ESI order. The Rule 26(d) discovery stay is not enforced, and significant discovery is encouraged before the conference. Typical schedule: discovery cutoff 90 or 120 days after the conference, witness lists (lay and expert) 45–60 days before the cutoff (the order’s summary page says 30 days), dispositive motions 30 or 45 days after the cutoff. No discovery is ordered after the cutoff. The parties may extend the discovery and dispositive

docs.x: Judge George Caram Steeh III, E.D. Mich.. docs.t: Judge George Caram Steeh III (E.D. Mich.) — Trial (trap)
docs.x: Judge George Caram Steeh III, E.D. Mich.. Trial (trap): The court uses a trailing docket; counsel must track earlier-scheduled cases in the Order Establishing Calendar for Trial. Trial adjournments are not typically granted but may be requested by letter giving the reason and opposing counsel’s position. Trial hours: the page says 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. (9 a.m. to 1 p.m. for trials over two weeks); the 6/18 order’s summary page says 9 a.m. to 1 p.m. daily. Exchange marked exhibits three days before trial (plaintiff numbers, defendant letters, under the 6/18 order) and provide two copies of an exhibit bench book; each side keeps custody of its admitted exhibits. Voir dire is conducted by the court and counsel. Jurors may take notes in complex cases and receive written copies of the instructions. Juror costs will typically be assessed in civil cases that settle on the day of jury selection or tr

docs.t: Judge George Caram Steeh III (E.D. Mich.) — Preliminary injunctions and TROs
docs.x: Judge George Caram Steeh III, E.D. Mich.. Preliminary injunctions and TROs: Ex parte injunctive relief is rarely granted; L.R. 7.1 and 65.1 and the judge’s Preliminary Injunction Hearing Procedures are strictly followed. Two hours are normally allotted for a hearing. Plaintiff’s counsel must promptly convene all counsel and distribute the procedures. Exhibits are pre-marked (plaintiff from 101, defendant from 501), and agreed exhibits are admitted at the outset. At least five business days before the hearing: plaintiff files a joint exhibit list with objections noted and a joint Rule 65(a)(2) consolidation statement and delivers exhibit copies to chambers; each party files a hearing brief (20-page limit) with numbered proposed findings and conclusions, a list of objected-to exhibits, and a witness list with brief summaries and time estimates. Exchange proposed findings in advance.

docs.x: Judge George Caram Steeh III, E.D. Mich.. ADR, ERISA, patent, and other matters: On stipulation the court refers cases to state-court case evaluation (the form uses the Wayne County Mediation Tribunal under MCR 2.403). The judge holds settlement conferences in jury cases on request; non-jury requests go to another judge or the magistrate judge. ERISA benefit-denial cases follow Wilkins: review on the administrative record, filed under seal as a joint appendix by defendant, discovery limited to procedural challenges, and cross motions for judgment (not Rule 56) with proposed findings and conclusions. docs.t: Judge Gershwin A. Drain (E.D. Mich.) — Font and page limits (trap)
docs.x: Judge Gershwin A. Drain, E.D. Mich.. Font and page limits (trap): Strict compliance with L.R. 5.1(a)(3): all text and footnotes at least 14 point (proportional) or 10-1/2 characters per inch (non-proportional). Noncompliant filings are immediately stricken. No extensions of the L.R. 7.1 page limit without a timely motion to extend; any filing over the limit will be stricken. Noncompliance with L.R. 5.1, 7.1, or the ECF Policies and Procedures may lead to denial of the motion.

docs.x: Judge Gershwin A. Drain, E.D. Mich.. Courtesy copies (trap): Deliver a copy of the complaint, answer, and all motions, briefs, responses, and replies directly to chambers. Two courtesy copies if a filing has more than ten exhibits. Copies must be properly bound; documents held by a rubber band or binder clip are not accepted. The scheduling order also requires a paper “Judge’s copy” of the proposed final pretrial order and proposed joint jury instructions (with disc).

docs.t: Judge Gershwin A. Drain (E.D. Mich.) — Motions
docs.x: Judge Gershwin A. Drain, E.D. Mich.. Motions: The court issues the notice of hearing and briefing schedule; movants need not submit one. Hearings are held on most motions, and discovery motions generally go to the magistrate judge. Strict compliance with L.R. 7.1(a) concurrence is required. Avoid boilerplate standard-of-review recitations and string cites; focus on a few recent, controlling cases. Support facts with record citations, attach unpublished or specialty-reporter opinions as exhibits, and supply cited deposition pages with enough surrounding pages for context. Only one summary judgment motion per party without leave. Citations must follow the latest Bluebook. If a pending motion is resolved before the hearing, notify chambers and file a notice of withdrawal.

docs.t: Judge Gershwin A. Drain (E.D. Mich.) — Scheduling conferences
docs.x: Judge Gershwin A. Drain, E.D. Mich.. Scheduling conferences: Notice of scheduling conference issues after the answer (after all defendants answer, if more than one). Rule 26(f) plan due 1 week before the conference. Counsel should discuss ADR with clients and agree to some form of it. Scheduling and status conferences are generally on Wednesdays; telephone appearance only for out-of-state counsel, arranged in advance. Final pretrial conferences are typically on Mondays. Typical schedule: witness lists (lay and expert) 6 weeks before discovery closes; discovery 4, 6, or 9 months out; dispositive motions 3 weeks after discovery closes; final pretrial order 12 weeks after that.

docs.t: Judge Gershwin A. Drain (E.D. Mich.) — Discovery and deadlines (trap)
docs.x: Judge Gershwin A. Drain, E.D. Mich.. Discovery and deadlines (trap): The court does not enforce the Rule 26(d) stay pending the Rule 26(f) conference. Rule 26(a)(1) disclosures are required. The discovery deadline may be extended by stipulation only if it does not affect the motion cutoff, final pretrial conference, or trial dates; any other change needs a timely written motion showing good cause.

docs.x: Judge Gershwin A. Drain, E.D. Mich.. Removal and TROs: Removed cases are reviewed and an order to show cause issues if jurisdiction is questionable. TROs follow Rule 65; ex parte relief only in extraordinary circumstances, with accelerated briefing and hearings set as urgency requires.

Civil motions in limine are due 4 weeks before the final pretrial confere

docs.t: Judge Gershwin A. Drain (E.D. Mich.) — Jury instructions and trial submissions
docs.x: Judge Gershwin A. Drain, E.D. Mich.. Jury instructions and trial submissions: At least 1 week before trial: voir dire requests, a single set of stipulated jury instructions (double spaced, with authority), a single proposed verdict form, each party’s separately filed disputed instructions, and a statement of claims or defenses of no more than 2 pages to be read to the jury. Alford pleas are rare and never accepted over government objection; nolo contendere pleas may be considered. Witness lists (with time estimates), proposed voir dire, stipulated jury instructions, and verdict form go directly to chambers, not e-filed. Notices contesting foundation, chain of custody, or scientific analysis are due with motions in limine, with a good-faith basis per item; otherwise foundation of inspected exhibits is deemed established. Witnesses, including law enforcement, testify in plain clothes. The defendant must attend the final pretrial conference. Witness unavailability is not a ground for continuance.

docs.t: Judge Mark A. Goldsmith (E.D. Mich.) — Concurrence certification (trap)
docs.x: Judge Mark A. Goldsmith, E.D. Mich.. Concurrence certification (trap): The first paragraph of every motion must certify L.R. 7.1(a) compliance with one of four statements (or one substantially similar): counsel spoke or met with opposing counsel, who expressly denied concurrence; counsel wrote to opposing counsel, who expressly denied concurrence; counsel wrote and 3 business days passed without express agreement; or counsel made no or a limited attempt because of exceptional circumstances stated with specificity. Modify the statement where a party is unrepresented. A motion without the certification will be struck.

docs.t: Judge Mark A. Goldsmith (E.D. Mich.) — Briefing (trap)

Only one response and one reply. Sur-replies, supplemental briefs, notices, or other papers in response to a motion without leave will be stricken, and a response may not be combined with a counter-motion. All supporting materials go in an appendix with a table of contents, tabbed exhibits, and relevant portions highlighted, plus the full text of unpublished authority not on Westlaw. Cite with page references, and for transcripts provide the cited pages with enough context. Cite unpublished cases to Westlaw, not Lexis. No courtesy copies

docs.t: Judge Mark A. Goldsmith (E.D. Mich.) — Summary judgment (trap)
docs.x: Judge Mark A. Goldsmith, E.D. Mich.. Summary judgment (trap): One summary judgment motion per party without leave, and challenges to several counts go in a single motion. The brief must open with a “Statement of Material Facts” in numbered paragraphs, each with specific record citations. The response opens with a “Counter-statement of Material Facts” using the same numbering, admitting or contesting each fact with record citations, and may add a “Statement of Additional Material Facts.” If it does, the reply opens with a “Reply to Counter-statement of Material Facts.” All of these fact statements count toward the page limit; no other fact recitation is required.

docs.t: Judge Mark A. Goldsmith (E.D. Mich.) — Discovery and deadlines
docs.x: Judge Mark A. Goldsmith, E.D. Mich.. Discovery and deadlines: Unless page 1 of the order says otherwise, parties may not be added or pleadings amended more than 14 days after the scheduling order, absent good cause. Witness lists (separating will-call from may-call) and exhibit lists are filed, and exhibits are exchanged by the exhibit-list date. “Expert” includes non-retained experts such as treating physicians; generic witness categories are not allowed. Experts must be available for deposition within 14 days after their disclosures. Serve discovery early enough for responses before the cutoff; no discovery after the cutoff absent good cause. Move to compel promptly once grounds appear and efforts to resolve are exhausted.

docs.t: Judge Mark A. Goldsmith (E.D. Mich.) — Adjournments, stipulated orders, and contact (trap)
docs.x: Judge Mark A. Goldsmith, E.D. Mich.. Adjournments, stipulated orders, and contact (trap): Events before the dispositive and expert motion deadline may be adjourned by proposed stipulated order, so long as no later date moves. Anything on or after that deadline requires a prompt written motion showing good cause, except that a request may be emailed to the case manager (copying opposing counsel) within 1 week after the order issues. Proposed and stipulated orders are not e-filed; submit them through CM/ECF Utilities in Word or WordPerfect. Counsel may contact the case manager only on administrative or scheduling matters, and may not contact law clerks unless expressly authorized.

docs.t: Judge Mark A. Goldsmith (E.D. Mich.) — Sealing and protective orders
docs.x: Judge Mark A. Goldsmith, E.D. Mich.. Sealing and protective orders: Proposed protective orders must include the judge’s required sealing language (no advance authorization; a motion or stipulated order under L.R. 5.3 stating authority, items, reasons, inadequacy of alternatives, and legal authority). With a motion to seal, submit a proposed order stating the particular reason through Utilities to the district judge or the referred magistrate judge. If granted, e-file the documents with a sealed designation.

docs.t: Judge Mark A. Goldsmith (E.D. Mich.) — Motions in limine and trial objections (trap)
docs.x: Judge Mark A. Goldsmith, E.D. Mich.. Motions in limine and trial objections (trap): Each party may file only one motion in limine (up to 25 pages) absent leave, by the “all other motions” deadline. Unresolved objections go in a separate motion (motion and response up to 15 pages each, attaching the exhibits) filed by that deadline, or they are waived. De bene esse depositions must be finished at least 21 days before that deadline, with page-and-line designations served at least 14 days before it. Unresolved objections go in a separate motion (up to 15 pages) by the deadline, or they are waived.

docs.t: Judge Mark A. Goldsmith (E.D. Mich.) — Settlement and ADR
docs.x: Judge Mark A. Goldsmith, E.D. Mich.. Settlement and ADR: The court conducts settlement conferences in jury cases and refers non-jury cases to another judicial officer. Trial counsel, natural-person parties, representatives with full and final authority for other parties and controlling insurers, and an authorized representative of any governmental party must attend in person; phone availability or counsel’s claimed authority does not satisfy this. Facilitation with a facilitator of the parties’ choosing is encouraged; the court picks one if the parties cannot agree. Case evaluation under L.R. 16.3 is by the court’s form order submitted through Utilities and must finish, including the accept/reject period, at least 7 days before the final pretrial conference.

List witnesses with the specific subject matter of their testimony and expert opinions with particularity, list exhibits by offering party with any pending objection motion, and identify other evidentiary issues with good cause for not raising them by motion in limine. docs.t: Judge Mark A. Goldsmith (E.D. Mich.) — Trial
docs.x: Judge Mark A. Goldsmith, E.D. Mich.. Trial: Trial dates are set in every civil case and not adjourned absent good cause. Trials generally run 8:30 a.m. to 1:00 p.m., with occasional afternoon sessions. The court conducts voir dire and allows follow-up questions by counsel. Jurors may take notes and ask witnesses questions, and the court sets time limits on openings and closings after consulting counsel. Each party submits a binder of its proposed exhibits, with exhibit lists that include “Admitted?” and “Notes” columns, at least 2 business days before trial. Counsel keep custody of admitted exhibits, provide a copy for every juror when publishing, and give the court a complete admitted set before deliberations. Trial briefs are optional (at least 7 days before trial). Disclose electronic display aids by the final pretrial conference and supply the equipment. The court gives customary ope

docs.t: Judge Mark A. Goldsmith (E.D. Mich.) — Patent cases and removal
docs.x: Judge Mark A. Goldsmith, E.D. Mich.. Patent cases and removal: Patent cases follow the judge’s Model Rule 26(f) Report and timeline, with trial about 24–26 months after the scheduling conference and liability and damages normally bifurcated before the same jury. A default protective order is entered automatically, and an off-the-record technology tutorial precedes claim construction briefing. Opening and response claim construction briefs are limited to 30 pages and the reply to 7. Live testimony at the Markman hearing requires a written motion and is typically limited to one hour per side. After removal, each party must re-file its state-court answers, pleadings, pending motions, and related responses and replies as separate docket entries; unre-filed state motions are generally not considered.

docs.x: Judge Matthew F. Leitman, E.D. Mich.. Courtesy copies (trap): Page: courtesy copies of all dispositive motions, responses, and replies, mailed no later than 1 business day after e-filing. Include copies of the main supporting cases (Westlaw printouts strongly preferred; no boilerplate authority) and all exhibits, printed double sided with the relevant parts highlighted and file stamps on the exhibits. The older sample civil and criminal orders require courtesy copies of all motions and briefs, sent the same day by first-class mail or hand-delivered by the next business day; the civil sample bars rubber bands and binder clips, and the criminal one bars prong fasteners.

Extensions of time or extra pages require a concise stipulation and order filed at least 1 week before the brief is due. If the parties resolve a pending motion, or the case settles, notify chambers in writing by the next business day by email to the case manager or by fax.

docs.t: Judge Matthew F. Leitman (E.D. Mich.) — Chambers contact and orders
docs.x: Judge Matthew F. Leitman, E.D. Mich.. Chambers contact and orders: No ex parte communications. Contact the case manager or judicial assistant only on procedural, administrative, or scheduling matters; contacting law clerks is not permitted unless authorized. Proposed and stipulated orders are not e-filed; submit them in Word through CM/ECF Utilities. No pro hac vice admission; non-Michigan bar members must have local counsel.

docs.x: Judge Matthew F. Leitman, E.D. Mich.. docs.t: Judge Matthew F. Leitman (E.D. Mich.) — TROs and preliminary injunctions
docs.x: Judge Matthew F. Leitman, E.D. Mich.. TROs and preliminary injunctions: The court strictly follows Rule 65 and LR 65.1 and rarely grants a TRO without notice. docs.t: Judge Matthew F. Leitman (E.D. Mich.) — Removal (trap)
docs.x: Judge Matthew F. Leitman, E.D. Mich.. Unresolved state-court motions not re-filed will not be considered, and LR 7.1(e) governs any remaining briefing. Remand motions for procedural defects must be filed within 30 days of the notice of removal; oral argument is typically held. Removal concerns are raised by order to show cause.

docs.t: Judge Matthew F. Leitman (E.D. Mich.) — Protective orders and sealing
docs.x: Judge Matthew F. Leitman, E.D. Mich.. docs.t: Judge Matthew F. Leitman (E.D. Mich.) — Settlement
docs.x: Judge Matthew F. Leitman, E.D. Mich.. Settlement: The court routinely holds at least one settlement conference and expects settlement discussions throughout. A brief status conference on settlement is held shortly after discovery closes, and parties may stipulate to case evaluation or mediation at any time.

docs.x: Judge Matthew F. Leitman, E.D. Mich.. Criminal cases: Counsel meet and confer within 10 days of arraignment, or the government files the 03-AO-027 discovery notice. docs.t: Judge Nancy G. Edmunds (E.D. Mich.) — Motions and hearings (trap)
docs.x: Judge Nancy G. Edmunds, E.D. Mich.. Motions and hearings (trap): The clerk sends the hearing notice; no briefing schedule is issued. Motions are heard about two months after filing. L.R. 7.1 response and reply deadlines are enforced even when the hearing is far off (timely extension requests are routinely granted), and a party that fails to respond on time may not argue. Replies are accepted under L.R. 7.1; sur-replies are not permitted. Strict L.R. 7.1(a) concurrence is required, and the court may impose costs for noncompliance. Proposed orders at the hearing are encouraged. To exceed 25 pages, file an ex parte application with a copy of the proposed brief; extensions are rarely more than 5 extra pages for responses and 2 for replies.

docs.t: Judge Nancy G. Edmunds (E.D. Mich.) — Summary judgment
docs.x: Judge Nancy G. Edmunds, E.D. Mich.. Summary judgment: Support each fact in the statement of material facts with citations to pleadings, discovery, depositions, affidavits, or documents, and file the full text of cited sources as an indexed appendix. Skip boilerplate standards and string cites; focus on a few recent, controlling cases. Copies of main cases with relevant passages highlighted and tabbed are encouraged, and copies of unpublished or specialty-reporter opinions must be submitted with the brief. Cite depositions by page and line; complete transcripts are encouraged.

docs.t: Judge Nancy G. Edmunds (E.D. Mich.) — Discovery
docs.x: Judge Nancy G. Edmunds, E.D. Mich.. Discovery: Discovery generally runs 3 to 6 months from the answer. All witnesses, lay and expert, must be disclosed 1 month before the discovery cutoff. Discovery motions are generally referred to the magistrate judge (no blanket referral); after referral, communicate only with that chambers. The court will not order discovery after the cutoff. Discovery may be extended by stipulation, before or after the cutoff and without a motion, only if the motion cutoff, final pretrial conference, and trial dates are unaffected; other changes need a timely written motion. The court may take telephone calls on disputes arising during a deposition.

docs.t: Judge Nancy G. Edmunds (E.D. Mich.) — Conferences, removal, and TROs
docs.x: Judge Nancy G. Edmunds, E.D. Mich.. Conferences, removal, and TROs: A scheduling conference sets cutoffs and pretrial, trial, pretrial-order, and instruction dates. Status and pretrial conferences may be by telephone for out-of-town counsel, and otherwise with prior approval. The court does not remand sua sponte (L.R. 81.1); an order to show cause issues if removal looks improper, and oral argument is typically held on remand motions. For TROs and preliminary injunctions, the court consults counsel and sets a shortened schedule by written order.

docs.t: Judge Nancy G. Edmunds (E.D. Mich.) — Mediation and settlement
docs.x: Judge Nancy G. Edmunds, E.D. Mich.. Mediation and settlement: Diversity cases are not routinely sent to L.R. 16.3 mediation; referral occurs after the discovery cutoff only if the parties stipulate to mediation sanctions, by the scheduling-order date, and counsel must complete mediation before the final pretrial conference. The judge routinely participates in settlement in jury cases and refers non-jury cases to another judge. Settlement is discussed at the final pretrial conference, and a settlement conference can be requested at any stage.

docs.t: Judge Nancy G. Edmunds (E.D. Mich.) — Final pretrial order and conference (trap)
docs.x: Judge Nancy G. Edmunds, E.D. Mich.. Final pretrial order and conference (trap): Counsel confer face to face; plaintiff drafts the joint final pretrial order under L.R. 16.2. The scheduling order requires it at least 1 week before the final pretrial conference, with an original and one copy to chambers. Pending motions needing pretrial decision must be flagged by then. Witness-list additions are allowed only in exceptional circumstances. Parties must attend the final pretrial conference with trial counsel, who must have full authority to discuss settlement without further client approval, unless other arrangements are approved in advance. The conference is typically 1 to 2 weeks before trial. Foundation or authenticity objections not raised before trial are waived.

docs.t: Judge Nancy G. Edmunds (E.D. Mich.) — Trial submissions (trap)
docs.x: Judge Nancy G. Edmunds, E.D. Mich.. Trial submissions (trap): Motions in limine: the page says at the final pretrial conference or 2 weeks before trial, whichever comes first; the scheduling order says 1 week before the trial term. Jury instructions: the page says the court gives counsel its standard opening and closing instructions at the final pretrial conference, and the joint instructions, joint verdict form, and separate disputed instructions (with each side’s support or objection) are due on the first day of trial, on paper and electronically. The scheduling order instead requires stipulated instructions 1 week before trial. At least 1 week before trial: voir dire requests and a statement of claims or defenses of no more than 2 pages. Bench trials: proposed findings and conclusions are filed before trial (the order says 1 week before), on paper and electronically.

docs.t: Judge Nancy G. Edmunds (E.D. Mich.) — Trial
docs.x: Judge Nancy G. Edmunds, E.D. Mich.. Trial: Trailing docket; report trial conflicts as soon as discovered (the earliest notice has priority). Hours are set week by week. Openings and closings are limited to 30–60 minutes, and repetitive or cumulative evidence may be limited. Ask permission to approach a witness or the bench; bench conferences are discouraged. Exchange exhibits 1 week before trial; bench book required. The page says plaintiff numbers from 1 and defendant from 500 (the order says each party starts at 1); traditional stickers preferred. Parties keep custody of exhibits during trial and pending appeal. Resolve evidentiary and foundation issues before trial; do not bring record keepers when business-record authenticity is not really disputed. Trial will not be adjourned for last-minute depositions.

docs.t: Judge Nancy G. Edmunds (E.D. Mich.) — Jury selection
docs.x: Judge Nancy G. Edmunds, E.D. Mich.. Jury selection: Strike method; the court conducts voir dire with limited follow-up by counsel, and counsel may not ask about the amount of damages sought. Three peremptories per party in civil cases, exercised in open court; a pass counts as an exercise. No alternates in civil trials; all seated jurors deliberate. The jury is charged before closing arguments and gets copies of the instructions. Juror questionnaires are allowed on motion for good cause.

docs.t: Judge Nancy G. Edmunds (E.D. Mich.) — Criminal cases
docs.x: Judge Nancy G. Edmunds, E.D. Mich.. Criminal cases: One or two alternates; defendant 10 peremptories, government 6. Pretrial conferences and arraignments on information are typically referred to a magistrate judge. Trial briefs are welcome but not required, and early Jencks disclosure is urged. Alford and nolo contendere pleas are rare and never accepted over government objection. Guideline disputes are typically resolved at a hearing before sentencing, and self-reporting is typically permitted.

docs.x: Judge Paul D. Borman, E.D. Mich.. Courtesy copies (trap): Courtesy hard copies are always required. No top fasteners, prong fasteners, side staples, loose pages, or single binder clips; a three-ring binder is preferred, though a short filing may be stapled in the top left corner or bound on the side. docs.t: Judge Paul D. Borman (E.D. Mich.) — Briefs and format (trap)
docs.x: Judge Paul D. Borman, E.D. Mich.. Briefs and format (trap): All filings, including exhibits, must be in 14-point font (L.R. 5.1(a)(3)). No string citations without at least parenthetical explanation; focus on a few recent, controlling cases. Ex parte applications to exceed 25 pages are rarely granted.

docs.t: Judge Paul D. Borman (E.D. Mich.) — Motion practice
docs.x: Judge Paul D. Borman, E.D. Mich.. Motion practice: Strict compliance with L.R. 7.1(a) concurrence; the court will strike papers and impose costs for noncompliance. Proposed and stipulated orders go through CM/ECF Utilities/Proposed Orders and are not docketed. TROs and preliminary injunctions: the court sets the schedule and, absent extraordinary circumstances, requires some notice to the other side and a chance for both sides to be heard. docs.x: Judge Paul D. Borman, E.D. Mich.. docs.t: Judge Paul D. Borman (E.D. Mich.) — ERISA benefits cases
docs.x: Judge Paul D. Borman, E.D. Mich.. ERISA benefits cases: Review is on the administrative record under Wilkins, and Rule 56 procedures are not used. Each party files a “Statement of Procedural Challenge” or “Statement of No Procedural Challenge” 3 weeks after the order; a procedural challenge suspends later deadlines pending a conference on limited discovery. Defendant serves the administrative record (with the plan and summary plan description) in 3 weeks; standard-of-review statements are due in 1 month; cross-motions to reverse or affirm, with a joint appendix, are due in 4 months; responses 1 month later and replies 2 weeks after that. docs.t: Judge Paul D. Borman (E.D. Mich.) — Criminal and compassionate release
docs.x: Judge Paul D. Borman, E.D. Mich.. Criminal and compassionate release: Pretrial matters are generally not referred to a magistrate judge. No criminal trial brief is required, and the government is urged to disclose Jencks material before trial. docs.x: Judge Robert Hardy Cleland, E.D. Mich.. Jurisdiction review (trap): The court reviews jurisdiction in every case. docs.t: Judge Audrey G. Fleissig (E.D. Mo.) — Informal matters and conferences
docs.x: Judge Audrey G. Fleissig, E.D. Mo.. Informal matters and conferences: No set time for informal matters (minor issues such as deadline changes or minor disputes). Notify opposing counsel, find out their availability, and call the judicial assistant to set an in-court or telephone conference. Most minor, agreed deadline changes can be handled by filing a motion to extend stating that opposing counsel consents; the judge rules on these as soon as possible. For an emergency motion needing a formal hearing on the record, call chambers. After the Case Management Order is entered, counsel may call chambers to set a scheduling or status conference or a conference call about problems keeping the case from moving forward.

docs.t: Judge Audrey G. Fleissig (E.D. Mo.) — Rule 16 conference (trap)
docs.x: Judge Audrey G. Fleissig, E.D. Mo.. Rule 16 conference (trap): Usually set after all defendants have answered or responded to the complaint; a party wanting it sooner must file a motion. Conferences are in person, usually in chambers (in the courtroom, on the record, when a party is pro se). Out-of-town counsel may participate by conference call but must give chambers contact information at least one business day before. Do not send an unprepared substitute or a lawyer who cannot commit on trial counsel’s calendar; be ready to discuss the facts, the Rule 16 Order’s topics, and settlement.

docs.t: Judge Audrey G. Fleissig (E.D. Mo.) — Discovery disputes (trap)
docs.x: Judge Audrey G. Fleissig, E.D. Mo.. Discovery disputes (trap): Before any discovery motion, the moving party must actually speak to opposing counsel, in person or by telephone, and certify the attempt in the motion; motions without the certification are denied without prejudice. If opposing counsel won’t return calls, detail those efforts in the certification. The judge either sets a hearing or rules on the papers. To request a hearing, say so in the motion or memorandum and call chambers once briefing is complete. For emergencies, call chambers for a preliminary telephone conference.

docs.t: Judge Audrey G. Fleissig (E.D. Mo.) — Expert disclosures (trap)
docs.x: Judge Audrey G. Fleissig, E.D. Mo.. Expert disclosures (trap): Non-retained experts (such as treating physicians and employees whose duties don’t regularly involve expert testimony) must be identified and given a Rule 26(a)(2)(C) summary of opinions and supporting facts, on the same date as the party’s other expert disclosures unless the CMO says otherwise. Undisclosed opinions may be excluded, and objections to sufficiency must be made promptly. Be ready at the Rule 16 conference to discuss expected expert types and the timing of reports and depositions; absent a stipulation, Rule 26 applies.

docs.t: Judge Audrey G. Fleissig (E.D. Mo.) — ADR
docs.x: Judge Audrey G. Fleissig, E.D. Mo.. ADR: Most civil cases are referred to mediation; be ready to discuss timing at the Rule 16 conference and consider what discovery is needed for a meaningful mediation. Once referred, ADR deadlines are binding and may be extended only by court order.

docs.t: Judge Audrey G. Fleissig (E.D. Mo.) — Trial setting and final pretrial conference
docs.x: Judge Audrey G. Fleissig, E.D. Mo.. Trial setting and final pretrial conference: Most cases are set on a firm three-week trial docket; assume your case is #1 unless told otherwise. St. Louis juries are picked at 9:00 a.m. or 1:15 p.m. on Mondays and Wednesdays. If the case is still on the docket two weeks before trial, chambers will call to set a final pretrial conference, normally two or three business days before trial; be ready to argue motions in limine there. For Cape Girardeau or Hannibal trials, the final pretrial conference is held in St. Louis unless you are told otherwise.

docs.t: Judge Audrey G. Fleissig (E.D. Mo.) — Voir dire and jury selection (trap)
docs.x: Judge Audrey G. Fleissig, E.D. Mo.. Voir dire and jury selection (trap): Before the case is called, supply an agreed, neutral brief statement of the case to read to the panel. Juror lists are not available in advance and must be returned to the clerk after selection. Attorneys usually conduct part of voir dire after the judge’s introductory questions; questions go to the panel as a whole first, with follow-ups to those who respond. No rapport-building questions, promises, speeches, argument, or talk about yourself. If the judge conducts all voir dire, proposed questions are due no later than two business days before trial. Challenges for cause are made outside the panel’s presence. Peremptories are exercised from the number to be seated plus total strikes, plaintiff first; in civil cases all remaining jurors deliberate and no alternates are designated.

docs.t: Judge Audrey G. Fleissig (E.D. Mo.) — Trial practice (trap)
docs.x: Judge Audrey G. Fleissig, E.D. Mo.. Trial practice (trap): Trial runs 9:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m.; preliminary matters may not be raised at the start of the day but are heard 30 minutes before start, at lunch, or at day’s end. Examine from the lectern; no permission is needed to hand a witness an exhibit, but don’t hover over the witness or jury. No recross as of right: approach the bench and state the areas sought, which must be new matter from redirect. Exhibits in opening need opposing counsel’s consent and advance notice to the judge. Pre-mark exhibits (plaintiffs numbers, defendants letters; defendants with more than 78 exhibits should use a scheme like AA, AB … rather than AAAAA). Bring a list of exhibits received without objection, show each exhibit to opposing counsel before a witness, and show demonstratives in advance of trial. docs.t: Judge Audrey G. Fleissig (E.D. Mo.) — Jury instructions
docs.x: Judge Audrey G. Fleissig, E.D. Mo.. Jury instructions: Eighth Circuit Model Instructions for boilerplate and covered matters; Missouri Approved Instructions (or another state’s) for state-law issues. Meet and confer and, whenever possible, submit one joint package. Submit two complete sets: a clean set headed only “Instruction No. ___” and a set showing source, offering party, and numbers. Give the court a clean copy on disk at the final pretrial conference. Without agreement, expect the instruction conference in the evening after the trial day.

docs.t: Judge Audrey G. Fleissig (E.D. Mo.) — Courtroom technology and decorum
docs.x: Judge Audrey G. Fleissig, E.D. Mo.. Courtroom technology and decorum: The judge strongly encourages using the evidence camera (ELMO). Schedule training (usually 30 minutes or less) with the Case Management Team before trial; none on the day of trial. Confer with the Clerk’s office before using your own computer, and bring your own audio tape player. Stand when speaking and when the jury enters; address witnesses and counsel by last name with titles (never first names, even clients); no food, gum, drinks other than water, or cell phone use; no expressions to the jury from counsel table; young children only with an adult seated with them in the gallery.

docs.t: Judge Catherine D. Perry (E.D. Mo.) — Scheduling, informal matters, and contact (trap)
docs.x: Judge Catherine D. Perry, E.D. Mo.. Scheduling, informal matters, and contact (trap): No regular informal matters docket. Most minor agreed deadline changes are handled by a written motion to extend stating that opposing counsel consents. Telephone conferences on scheduling disputes are sometimes available; notify opposing counsel before seeking one. For an emergency needing a formal hearing on the record, call chambers to schedule it. In civil cases, do not email the judge or chambers staff unless specifically told to. In criminal cases, counsel may email the Judicial Assistant, Brian Crow (brian_crow@moed.uscourts.gov), about scheduling and logistics only, not substance.

docs.t: Judge Catherine D. Perry (E.D. Mo.) — Courtesy copies and proposed orders
docs.x: Judge Catherine D. Perry, E.D. Mo.. Courtesy copies and proposed orders: Courtesy copies of bulky summary judgment motions are helpful; no courtesy copies of other filings are needed. Any courtesy copy must show the ECF header (document number, page number, and filing date) on every page. File proposed orders in ECF as an exhibit to the motion, and also email them in Word format to Brian Crow.

docs.t: Judge Catherine D. Perry (E.D. Mo.) — Discovery disputes (trap)
docs.x: Judge Catherine D. Perry, E.D. Mo.. Discovery disputes (trap): Before any discovery motion, meet and confer and certify that you did. Exchanging “nasty letters or emails” does not count, and the judge does not want them attached to motions; counsel must actually talk. If the opponent won’t return calls, say so in the certification. The judge either sets discovery motions for hearing or rules on the papers. For an emergency discovery dispute, schedule a telephone conference on the record.

docs.t: Judge Catherine D. Perry (E.D. Mo.) — Rule 16 conference and ADR
docs.x: Judge Catherine D. Perry, E.D. Mo.. Rule 16 conference and ADR: Civil Rule 16 conferences are usually set after all defendants answer; a party wanting one sooner must file a motion. Follow the Order Setting Rule 16 Conference and the Case Management Order. Come prepared to discuss the facts, everything in the Rule 16 order (including settlement), and likely types of expert witnesses. Do not send an unprepared substitute attorney. Most civil cases are referred to mediation; be ready to discuss timing of the referral at the Rule 16 conference.

docs.t: Judge Catherine D. Perry (E.D. Mo.) — Experts (trap)
docs.x: Judge Catherine D. Perry, E.D. Mo.. Experts (trap): Absent stipulation or CMO provisions, Rule 26(a)(2) governs disclosure. Experts are limited to opinions and bases disclosed in discovery (report or deposition) and, absent unusual circumstances, may not supplement or change opinions after expert discovery closes; CMO deadlines override different deadlines in rules or statutes. Expert reports are hearsay and usually not admitted (impeachment use is allowed). Do not “tender the witness as an expert” or ask the judge to tell the jury a witness is an expert, and do not ask witnesses whether they consider themselves experts. Experts may not opine on the law or sum up the evidence.

docs.t: Judge Catherine D. Perry (E.D. Mo.) — Trial settings and final pretrial conference (trap)
docs.x: Judge Catherine D. Perry, E.D. Mo.. Trial settings and final pretrial conference (trap): Most cases are set on a firm two-week trial docket mixing jury and non-jury, civil and criminal cases. Juries are picked at 9 a.m. and 1:15 p.m. on Mondays and Wednesdays in St. Louis. Unless told otherwise, assume you are #1 on the docket. Appear 30 minutes before scheduled jury selection for a final pretrial conference on evidentiary issues, motions in limine, and scheduling; an earlier, longer conference may be set or requested. In civil cases, exhibits not objected to in the pretrial submissions are received at the start of trial; bring a list of them. Order daily copy through the Case Management Team well in advance.

docs.t: Judge Catherine D. Perry (E.D. Mo.) — Voir dire
docs.x: Judge Catherine D. Perry, E.D. Mo.. Voir dire: The jury panel list (names, municipality, employers, occupation, and spouse’s employer and occupation) is handed out as jurors enter; it is not provided in advance. Return all copies after selection. After the judge’s introductory questions, counsel may conduct part of voir dire. Ask general questions of the whole panel, then follow up with those who respond. No speeches, arguing the case, seeking promises, or questions just to hear jurors speak; submit in writing any questions you want the judge to ask. Cause challenges are made outside the panel’s presence; plaintiff then defense make peremptories. In civil cases the first seven or eight remaining jurors are seated (all “real” jurors); in criminal cases the first twelve, with alternates depending on trial length.

docs.t: Judge Catherine D. Perry (E.D. Mo.) — Trial conduct (trap)
docs.x: Judge Catherine D. Perry, E.D. Mo.. Trial conduct (trap): Openings, examinations, and closings from the lectern; no permission needed to approach the witness, but never hover over the witness or jury. State objections by legal basis only, standing. No recross as of right: approach the bench and state the areas sought; allowed only if redirect raised something new. Pre-mark exhibits per the CMO (plaintiff/government numbers, defendants letters). Closing arguments presumptively 20 minutes; plaintiff or government must use more than 50% of its time in the opening part. Jurors may take notes. Evidence presentation equipment is expected to be used at all trials; schedule training (about 30 minutes) with the Case Management Team, and confer with the clerk’s office first if using your own computer.

docs.t: Judge Catherine D. Perry (E.D. Mo.) — Depositions and jury instructions
docs.x: Judge Catherine D. Perry, E.D. Mo.. Depositions and jury instructions: If you will read less than you designated, tell opposing counsel in advance so objections and counter-designations can be resolved; the judge expects disputes worked out first. Give advance notice of video depositions so objections can be ruled on in time for editing. The court reporter does not transcribe deposition testimony: you must provide a page-and-line list of what was actually read or shown. The judge uses 8th Circuit Model instructions for boilerplate and sends written instructions to the jury. Email Word versions of proposed instructions to Brian Crow.

docs.t: Judge Catherine D. Perry (E.D. Mo.) — Courtroom decorum
docs.x: Judge Catherine D. Perry, E.D. Mo.. Courtroom decorum: Stand when the jury enters and leaves and whenever speaking. Attorney phones silenced; client, witness, and spectator phones off. No photos or recording; laptops for audience members need advance approval. No food, drink other than water, or gum. Address witnesses and opposing counsel by last name and title, never first names, even your own client.

docs.t: Judge Cristian Stevens (E.D. Mo.) — Discovery disputes (trap)
docs.x: Judge Cristian Stevens, E.D. Mo.. Discovery disputes (trap): Comply with Local Rule 3.04 before any discovery motion or memorandum (including non-parties served with subpoenas); noncompliant filings will be denied. Letters, emails, or texts do not satisfy meet-and-confer. If unresolved, the parties must jointly file a single memorandum of no more than 3 pages requesting a conference, stating their attempts at resolution and concisely describing (e.g., in bullet points) the issues. Lead counsel or counsel with authority to resolve the dispute must appear in person at the discovery conference. With incarcerated pro se litigants, confer only in writing, and discovery motions may be filed without requesting a conference.

docs.t: Judge Cristian Stevens (E.D. Mo.) — Sealing and protective orders (trap)
docs.x: Judge Cristian Stevens, E.D. Mo.. Sealing and protective orders (trap): Local Rule 13.05 governs sealing in civil and criminal cases; the court strongly prefers redaction to sealing and requires a sufficient legal and factual basis (citing IDT Corp. v. eBay and Flynt v. Lombardi). Noncompliant protective orders and motions will be denied. A proposed protective order addressing sealed filings must require leave of court to file under seal and provide for lifting the seal at the end of the case. One addressing discovery disputes must expressly require the Requirement No. 7 discovery procedure.

docs.t: Judge Cristian Stevens (E.D. Mo.) — Motions and record citations (trap)
docs.x: Judge Cristian Stevens, E.D. Mo.. Motions and record citations (trap): Comply with Local Rule 4.01. Record citations must be consistent and, whenever possible, include the CM/ECF docket entry number; the court will not search the record. With numerous exhibits, file an “Exhibit Key” listing the docket entry for each exhibit (e.g., “Exhibit AA appears at Doc. [22-27].”). Duplicative filings are prohibited: parties with the same counsel moving on the same or similar grounds must file a single motion, memorandum, and statement of uncontroverted material facts; parties with different counsel are encouraged to coordinate.

docs.t: Judge Cristian Stevens (E.D. Mo.) — Extensions, unopposed motions, and CMO changes (trap)
docs.x: Judge Cristian Stevens, E.D. Mo.. Extensions, unopposed motions, and CMO changes (trap): Extension motions must state all parties’ positions, show in the title any prior requests (e.g., “Third Request for an Extension”), and cite and apply the legal standard (Fed. R. Civ. P. 6(b); Fed. R. Crim. P. 45(b)); consent alone is not enough. Label joint, unopposed, or consent motions as such in both the body and the CM/ECF title. To change a CMO term not amendable by stipulation under Rule 29, file a motion before the deadline, soliciting all parties’ consent.

docs.t: Judge Cristian Stevens (E.D. Mo.) — Rule 16 conference
docs.x: Judge Cristian Stevens, E.D. Mo.. Rule 16 conference: Usually set after all defendants have filed a responsive pleading; contact chambers to request an earlier one. Absent truly exceptional circumstances, lead counsel must appear in person, prepared on the facts and the joint scheduling plan.

docs.t: Judge Cristian Stevens (E.D. Mo.) — ADR
docs.x: Judge Cristian Stevens, E.D. Mo.. ADR: Most civil cases are referred to ADR, usually for about 60 days. Plaintiff’s counsel is lead counsel for coordinating ADR and must work with opposing counsel to select a neutral. Notify the court immediately upon settlement.

docs.t: Judge Cristian Stevens (E.D. Mo.) — AI and sanctions (trap)
docs.x: Judge Cristian Stevens, E.D. Mo.. AI and sanctions (trap): Filers are responsible for any AI-generated content under Rule 11. Any filing that hallucinates citations or misstates the law, or was not properly reviewed or reasonably investigated, “will result in” sanctions. Failure to comply with any part of the Requirements may draw sanctions ranging from fees and penalties to striking pleadings, dismissal, or default judgment (Local Rule 5.04).

docs.t: Judge Cristian Stevens (E.D. Mo.) — Withdrawal and e-filing
docs.x: Judge Cristian Stevens, E.D. Mo.. Withdrawal and e-filing: A motion to withdraw that leaves an individual unrepresented should include an affidavit showing the client’s consent; without consent, request an ex parte hearing. Create PDFs by printing or publishing to PDF, not by scanning paper copies, so they are text-searchable.

docs.t: Judge Cristian Stevens (E.D. Mo.) — Courtroom rules
docs.x: Judge Cristian Stevens, E.D. Mo.. Courtroom rules: On arrival, lead counsel reports to the courtroom deputy and introduces others; no one may speak without an entered appearance. Stand and speak into the lectern microphone; stand when the judge or jury enters or exits. No photos, recording, or broadcasting; laptops and tablets only at counsel tables; no food, gum, drinks other than water, or audible devices; phones off unless authorized in advance. Dress appropriately and tell clients and witnesses the rules.

docs.t: Judge Henry Autrey (E.D. Mo.) — Informals (trap)
docs.x: Judge Henry Autrey, E.D. Mo.. Informals (trap): All informal matters must be submitted in writing and filed in CM/ECF; they reach the judge within 24 hours of filing, and rulings go to counsel through CM/ECF. If an informal needs more immediate attention, or to request a conference, call the judicial assistant (Beverly Goff) or the Case Management Team (314-244-7533).

docs.t: Judge Henry Autrey (E.D. Mo.) — Trial docket (trap)
docs.x: Judge Henry Autrey, E.D. Mo.. Trial docket (trap): One-week trial docket: all cases are set on Monday and ride the docket for the week, so be ready for trial at any time during the setting week. Criminal cases take priority over civil. Cases are tried in the order best suited to the docket (considering age and anticipated length). If a case settles, the next case is expected to be ready. Bumped cases receive a new setting. Notify the Judicial Assistant or Team Leader well in advance if a case needs special attention.

docs.t: Judge Henry Autrey (E.D. Mo.) — Rule 16 conference
docs.x: Judge Henry Autrey, E.D. Mo.. Rule 16 conference: Usually in person; by telephone on the parties’ request if an attorney is more than 100 miles away (the court initiates the call). Conferences with a pro se party are held in the courtroom on the record. A proposed Joint Scheduling Plan is due no later than 10 days before the conference; plaintiff initiates the meeting and files it unless ordered otherwise. Lack of cooperation does not excuse filing; a separate plan must attach a memorandum explaining why a joint plan could not be filed.

docs.t: Judge Henry Autrey (E.D. Mo.) — Case management order changes (trap)
docs.x: Judge Henry Autrey, E.D. Mo.. Case management order changes (trap): Requests to change the CMO must be in writing and filed. Changes to trial dates and dispositive-motion deadlines are not routinely granted and need a statement of good cause.

docs.t: Judge Henry Autrey (E.D. Mo.) — Protective orders and sealing (trap)
docs.x: Judge Henry Autrey, E.D. Mo.. Protective orders and sealing (trap): Proposed protective orders must follow Local Rule 13.05 and include a date certain for lifting the seal or returning documents; a proposed order without one will be denied without prejudice.

docs.t: Judge Henry Autrey (E.D. Mo.) — ADR
docs.x: Judge Henry Autrey, E.D. Mo.. ADR: Civil cases (except habeas) are referred to ADR on the parties’ request. Plaintiff’s counsel (or agreed counsel) is lead counsel and must notify the clerk of the agreed neutral within twenty days of the referral’s start; ADR deadlines are binding and extendable only by court order. Notify the court immediately whether or not a settlement is reached; after settlement, file a Stipulation for Dismissal within thirty days.

docs.t: Judge Henry Autrey (E.D. Mo.) — Pretrial conference and voir dire
docs.x: Judge Henry Autrey, E.D. Mo.. Pretrial conference and voir dire: Pretrial conferences are discretionary; if required, held no later than seven (7) days before trial. After the court’s initial questions, counsel may conduct voir dire subject to time limits set at the pretrial conference. The court may conduct voir dire itself; then counsel are encouraged to submit questions no later than five (5) days before trial.

docs.t: Judge Henry Autrey (E.D. Mo.) — Jury Evidence System
docs.x: Judge Henry Autrey, E.D. Mo.. Jury Evidence System: The judge uses the Jury Evidence System for jury trials. Provide the clerk digital copies of all admitted exhibits: documents in Word or PDF, photos as JPEG, and videos as WMV or MP4.

docs.t: Judge Henry Autrey (E.D. Mo.) — Other
docs.x: Judge Henry Autrey, E.D. Mo.. Other: Patent cases: counsel should be familiar with the court’s Local Patent Rules. Schedule attorney admissions through the judicial assistant or Case Management Team, who also handle docket questions.

docs.x: Judge John Andrew Ross, E.D. Mo.. Scheduling, conferences, and contact: Most minor agreed deadline changes can be made by a motion to extend stating that opposing counsel consents. Criminal matters go to the judicial assistant; civil matters to the law clerks. Staff can discuss scheduling, logistics, procedure, and chambers preferences, but not substance.

docs.t: Judge John Andrew Ross (E.D. Mo.) — Rule 16 and case management
docs.x: Judge John Andrew Ross, E.D. Mo.. Rule 16 and case management: After all defendants answer, the court orders a joint proposed scheduling plan and enters a CMO based on it unless a party requests, or the court orders, a Rule 16 conference. Rule 16 conferences are in person in chambers unless ordered otherwise (in the courtroom, on the record, if a party is pro se). Out-of-town counsel may appear by Zoom or phone with prior approval. Don’t send an unprepared substitute or a lawyer who can’t commit on trial counsel’s calendar.

docs.t: Judge John Andrew Ross (E.D. Mo.) — Discovery disputes
docs.x: Judge John Andrew Ross, E.D. Mo.. Discovery disputes: Meet and confer and certify it in the motion (Local Rule 3.04); if your opponent won’t return calls, say so in the certification. The judge typically rules on the papers unless a hearing is needed; for emergencies, call chambers for a telephone conference.

docs.x: Judge John Andrew Ross, E.D. Mo.. Briefing and courtesy copies (trap): Include a Westlaw citation for unreported decisions. Mail or hand-deliver to chambers at 111 South Tenth Street, Suite 3N, St. Louis, MO 63102.

docs.x: Judge John Andrew Ross, E.D. Mo.. Generative AI (trap): Signers are fully responsible for GenAI-assisted content and must independently verify all quotations, citations, and analysis before filing. Do not put confidential litigation material (e.g., protected discovery or sealed documents) into GenAI tools that may retain, train on, or disclose it. Violations may draw sanctions.

docs.x: Judge John Andrew Ross, E.D. Mo.. ADR: Most civil cases are referred to mediation; when proposing a mediation date, consider the discovery needed and time to exchange it. Once referred, ADR deadlines are binding and may be extended only with the court’s approval.

docs.x: Judge Rodney W. Sippel, E.D. Mo.. Case management orders (trap): Civil and criminal CMO deadlines are strictly enforced. Modifications require a motion to amend and are granted only on a showing of exceptional circumstances.

docs.t: Judge Rodney W. Sippel (E.D. Mo.) — Final pretrial conference and jury instructions
docs.x: Judge Rodney W. Sippel, E.D. Mo.. Final pretrial conference and jury instructions: Appear 30 minutes before jury selection for an on-the-record final pretrial conference in the designated courtroom (8:30 for a 9:00 a.m. selection; 12:45 for 1:15 p.m.) on evidentiary issues, motions in limine, and scheduling. docs.t: Judge Rodney W. Sippel (E.D. Mo.) — Voir dire
docs.x: Judge Rodney W. Sippel, E.D. Mo.. Voir dire: The judge introduces and asks introductory questions; submit specific questions in writing. Cause challenges are made outside the panel’s presence; plaintiff then defense make strikes. Return all jury lists after selection.

docs.t: Judge Rodney W. Sippel (E.D. Mo.) — Trial conduct (trap)
docs.x: Judge Rodney W. Sippel, E.D. Mo.. No speaking objections: stand and state the legal basis in a word or phrase. Bench conferences and sidebars are disfavored; make record arguments at breaks. No recross as of right (only if redirect raised something new). Closings presumptively twenty minutes. Disclose witness identity and order at least 24 hours before the trial day they are called. Show each exhibit to opposing counsel before a witness, and show demonstratives and summaries before trial. Only one lawyer per party may question a witness. Disputes over tape-recording transcripts must be raised at least five (5) days before trial if counsel cannot resolve them.

docs.t: Judge Rodney W. Sippel (E.D. Mo.) — Courtroom decorum
docs.x: Judge Rodney W. Sippel, E.D. Mo.. Courtroom decorum: Notify the Deputy Clerk on arrival and introduce others. No comments, expressions, or signals toward the jury or witnesses; violators may be ejected, and signaling a testifying witness is treated as contempt. Children may watch only with an adult seated with them who is not a party, attorney, or case agent.

Motions for judicial notice or to declare an issue as a matter of law are entertained only if the parties contest the point; if it is uncontested, file a stipulation instead. Parties are expected to attend a settlement conference midway through discovery. A request to continue it because discovery is incomplete will not be granted absent good cause.

The court intends to end the conference with the case ready for trial and prefers record-making at recesses or before or after the trial day.
