docs.t: Judge Cynthia M. Rufe (E.D. Pa.) — Criminal motions and continuances (trap)
docs.x: Judge Cynthia M. Rufe, E.D. Pa.. Criminal motions and continuances (trap): Pretrial motions are due at least 30 days before trial; supporting memoranda (25 pages) as soon as possible and no later than the hearing. Co-defendants may not join each other’s motions without leave. Post-trial memoranda and responses are capped at 25 pages; replies and sur-replies need leave and are capped at 10 pages. Trial continuance motions are due at least 14 days before trial, with a proposed order containing a detailed Speedy Trial Act ends-of-justice finding (18 U.S.C. § 3161(h)(7)). No letter requests. The pretrial conference is at least 3 days before trial. The judge conducts extensive voir dire; counsel may ask follow-up questions.

docs.t: Judge Cynthia M. Rufe (E.D. Pa.) — Sentencing
docs.x: Judge Cynthia M. Rufe, E.D. Pa.. Sentencing: Sentencing continuances are for good cause only, and requests over 90 days are generally not considered. Any further continuance needs a joint written request showing good cause and, if granted, a joint written status update every 30 days. Sentencing motions are due 14 days before sentencing (responses 7 days before); sentencing memoranda 7 days before (responses 3 days before).

docs.t: Judge Gail A. Weilheimer (E.D. Pa.) — Meet and confer before motions (trap)
docs.x: Judge Gail A. Weilheimer, E.D. Pa.. Meet and confer before motions (trap): Before any discovery motion, Rule 12(b) motion, or other dispositive motion, the movant must confer with opposing counsel by substantive verbal communication (letters or emails don’t count) at least 5 days before filing, discuss the substance, and offer a chance to cure. A report that opposing counsel was unavailable or that reasonable efforts were made is insufficient. If unresolved, file a certification with the motion giving the date(s) and length of the discussion and a one-sentence description of each issue; each counsel should sign and date it. The court will deny a 12(b)(6), (e), or (f) motion or discovery motion that doesn’t comply, and a party that fails to respond to conferral attempts may be sanctioned. An amended complaint filed to cure deficiencies raised in the conference, with a certification attach

docs.t: Judge Gail A. Weilheimer (E.D. Pa.) — Motions and briefs (trap)
docs.x: Judge Gail A. Weilheimer, E.D. Pa.. Motions and briefs (trap): Briefs supporting or opposing a motion are limited to 25 pages (motions in limine excepted); leave to exceed requires a motion filed before the deadline showing good cause. Use 12-point Times New Roman, double spacing, one-inch margins, and numbered pages; all PDFs must be text-searchable. No reply briefs without leave. Move for leave within 5 days of the response, email a courtesy copy to chambers, highlight the specific issues needing reply, and do not attach a proposed reply. The court rules without a response and the order sets the reply’s scope and due date. File each exhibit as a separately numbered attachment with an objective, descriptive title (e.g., “6/14/19 Deposition of John Doe”). Oral argument is scheduled only when it helps the court; motions are frequently decided on the papers even if argument is requested.

docs.t: Judge Gail A. Weilheimer (E.D. Pa.) — Courtesy copies
docs.x: Judge Gail A. Weilheimer, E.D. Pa.. Courtesy copies: When exhibits or attachments to any filing exceed 20 pages, deliver one hard copy of the exhibits to chambers within 48 hours of docketing. More than two exhibits go in a binder, tabbed, with a table of contents matching the filing. For a Joint Statement of Undisputed Facts the moving party provides the copy; for cross-motions the parties agree who does (plaintiff if they can’t agree).

docs.t: Judge Gail A. Weilheimer (E.D. Pa.) — Summary judgment (trap)
docs.x: Judge Gail A. Weilheimer, E.D. Pa.. Summary judgment (trap): At least 28 days before moving, all parties must meet and confer on a neutral Joint Statement of Undisputed Facts, with exhibits, covering every undisputed fact any party will rely on; relevance or materiality is no reason to exclude a fact. If no agreement is reached, the movant must certify that. If briefing shows the parties actually agreed on enough material facts, the court may hold a hearing on sanctions or reject the filings and require a revised Joint Statement. Absent a scheduling-order deadline, oppositions are due in 30 days.

docs.t: Judge Gail A. Weilheimer (E.D. Pa.) — Communication, extensions, and sealing
docs.x: Judge Gail A. Weilheimer, E.D. Pa.. Substantive communications must be docketed. Extensions, even joint or unopposed, require a motion on the docket showing good cause, made as early as possible; requests on the deadline day are typically denied. Exceptions: a filed joint stipulation (with a judge’s signature line) extending time to answer or move against an initial complaint by no more than 30 days, and unfiled agreements extending discovery deadlines that don’t alter the dispositive motion deadline. docs.t: Judge Gail A. Weilheimer (E.D. Pa.) — Rule 16 conference and discovery (trap)
docs.x: Judge Gail A. Weilheimer, E.D. Pa.. Rule 16 conference and discovery (trap): The Rule 16 conference is held as soon as possible after all defendants answer (contact chambers if not scheduled in a reasonable time). Lead trial counsel must attend (or substitute counsel with deep knowledge of the case if lead counsel is on trial), ready to address substance, settlement, and scheduling. A joint Rule 26(f) report in the judge’s format (a separate patent format exists) is due 5 days before. Discovery starts when the order scheduling the Rule 16 conference issues, not at the conference, and the discovery period runs from that order; it should normally end 90–120 days from that notice. The report form asks for initial disclosures already produced, signed authorizations (e.g., HIPAA), insurance details with the policy attached, and the latest demand and offer in jury cases only. Straightforward d

docs.t: Judge Gail A. Weilheimer (E.D. Pa.) — Removed cases (trap)
docs.x: Judge Gail A. Weilheimer, E.D. Pa.. Removed cases (trap): If the notice of removal didn’t attach the state court complaint as a separately named exhibit, file an Amended Notice of Removal doing so; this doesn’t change deadlines. docs.t: Judge Gail A. Weilheimer (E.D. Pa.) — Settlement
docs.x: Judge Gail A. Weilheimer, E.D. Pa.. Settlement: Request a settlement conference by letter or email when all parties sincerely want one. Bench trials go to Magistrate Judge Lynne Sitarski or the court’s mediation program. In jury cases, Judge Weilheimer may conduct the conference only if all parties agree, in writing or on the record, that the judge may keep presiding if it fails. Conferences with Judge Weilheimer are in the courthouse with everyone with settlement authority present. Email a confidential settlement memorandum (not docketed or shared) with case strengths and weaknesses, critical documents, the latest offer and demand, settlement authority, and other helpful information. The Guidelines say 7 days before; the separate requirements sheet says at least 5 days.

docs.t: Judge Gail A. Weilheimer (E.D. Pa.) — Pretrial conference and motions in limine (trap)
docs.x: Judge Gail A. Weilheimer, E.D. Pa.. Pretrial conference and motions in limine (trap): Held after dispositive motions are decided (or if none are filed); lead trial counsel (or deeply knowledgeable substitute) must attend, and the court conducts settlement negotiations as part of it (parties not attending in person must be available by phone). A date-certain trial is usually set 60–90 days out. At least 7 days before, each counsel dockets a Pretrial Conference Memorandum: narrative of up to 3 double-spaced pages, witness list with up to two sentences per witness, exhibit list, stipulations, trial length, unavailable dates, damages claimed, the latest settlement negotiations (jury cases only), and whether the parties want an in-person settlement conference. Unlisted witnesses and exhibits may be precluded. Only verified conflicts count as unavailability (trial attachment, scheduled medical

docs.t: Judge Gail A. Weilheimer (E.D. Pa.) — Trial (trap)
docs.x: Judge Gail A. Weilheimer, E.D. Pa.. Trial (trap): Trial dates are continued only for verified, truly emergency circumstances. The judge has no assigned courtroom; chambers gives the assignment at least 1 week before trial. Ask chambers whether you must bring your own technology. Bring 3 copies of all exhibits in pre-marked, tabbed three-ring binders with a 12-point table of contents in table format (number, description, identified, admitted); a joint binder is preferred. To show exhibits in opening, you need agreement or leave: give the list at least 5 business days before openings; objections are due 3 business days before (failure may waive); meet and confer 2 business days before and tell the court by close of business that day if a ruling is needed. Bad-faith objections or use of plainly objectionable documents may be sanctioned. Stand to address the court; counsel may sit or move ab

docs.t: Judge Gail A. Weilheimer (E.D. Pa.) — Pro hac vice and newer attorneys
docs.x: Judge Gail A. Weilheimer, E.D. Pa.. Pro hac vice and newer attorneys: While a pro hac vice motion is pending, local counsel must attend every appearance, including phone and video. If pro hac vice counsel shows unfamiliarity with the Local Rules or the judge’s protocols, the court may require local counsel at all appearances or revoke admission. The judge encourages letting newer associates argue; notify the court at sidebar or by email in advance with the associate’s and supervising counsel’s names, and supervising counsel may supplement.

docs.t: Judge Gail A. Weilheimer (E.D. Pa.) — Patent cases
docs.x: Judge Gail A. Weilheimer, E.D. Pa.. Patent cases: The patent Rule 26(f) form adds a default schedule (initial contentions 1–2 weeks before the Rule 16 conference), an interim outside-counsel-only protective order, and disclosure of licenses and settlement agreements by the Rule 16 conference. Motions to compel require a conference with the court first. Claim construction: briefs are served, not filed, then combined into one Joint Claim Construction Brief term by term; a party proposing “plain and ordinary meaning” must explain it, and failing to propose a function and structure for an arguable means-plus-function term waives it. No Markman testimony without prior approval; absent other agreement, plaintiff picks the first term and sides alternate. Expert-report timeliness or scope objections must be raised within one week of the report or are waived; Daubert motions are due by the dispos

docs.t: Judge Jerry Pappert (E.D. Pa.) — Generative AI disclosure (trap)
docs.x: Judge Jerry Pappert, E.D. Pa.. Generative AI disclosure (trap): Anyone who uses generative AI to prepare a filing must disclose that use, identify precisely which portions contain generated content, identify the tool and how it was used, and certify that every citation to the law or record was verified under Rule 11. Noncompliance may bring referral to the court’s Disciplinary Committee or a state bar, striking of the filing, monetary sanctions, or other sanctions.

docs.t: Judge Jerry Pappert (E.D. Pa.) — Briefs and motions (trap)
docs.x: Judge Jerry Pappert, E.D. Pa.. Briefs and motions (trap): Briefs are capped at 25 double-spaced pages in 12-point font, excluding tables and exhibits; any brief over 10 pages needs a table of contents and table of authorities. Footnotes are discouraged and should not contain citations. Noncompliant briefs may be stricken. To exceed 25 pages, move before the deadline; a pending motion does not extend the deadline. Put all grounds in one comprehensive motion (for example, not separate motions to dismiss per count). Replies are due within 7 days of the opposition, capped at 10 pages, and limited to new issues; no replies on motions in limine. Sur-replies need leave on motion.

docs.t: Judge Jerry Pappert (E.D. Pa.) — Exhibits and summary judgment
docs.x: Judge Jerry Pappert, E.D. Pa.. Exhibits and summary judgment: File each exhibit as a separately numbered attachment titled with an objective description (for example, “6/14/19 Deposition of John Doe”). Text-searchable exhibits are encouraged. Rule 56 motions need a numbered statement of material facts with specific record citations; the opposition must respond paragraph by paragraph and may add numbered additional facts. Uncontroverted facts are deemed admitted, and failure to cite the record may defeat relief. Motions and responses need an exhibit index. The judge will rarely, if ever, grant summary judgment in a non-jury case.

docs.t: Judge Jerry Pappert (E.D. Pa.) — Hearings, argument, and contact
docs.x: Judge Jerry Pappert, E.D. Pa.. Hearings, argument, and contact: No set days for argument or evidentiary hearings; the judge schedules them when warranted. Request oral argument by letter or in the motion or response. In criminal cases argument on a substantive motion is generally allowed on request. Correspondence is allowed only on scheduling, discovery disputes, routine matters, or settlement; all else must be filed. Calls go to Courtroom Deputy Katie Rolon, 267-299-7530; never contact law clerks. Raise matters only after discussing them with opposing counsel, and be ready to state their position. For telephone conferences, the moving party (in criminal cases, the U.S. Attorney’s Office) initiates the call and contacts the deputy once all are on. No cell phones.

docs.t: Judge Jerry Pappert (E.D. Pa.) — Rule 16 and continuances (trap)
docs.x: Judge Jerry Pappert, E.D. Pa.. Rule 16 and continuances (trap): The Rule 16 conference is set shortly after all defendants answer. Submit a joint Rule 26(f) report with discovery plan to chambers at least 3 business days before. Parties who skip a substantive 26(f) meeting have no voice at the conference and may be sanctioned. Lead trial counsel must attend, with authority to discuss everything including settlement, and be ready on all claims, defenses, and L.R. 16.1(b) and Rule 16 and 26(a) topics. The trial date is set at the Rule 16 conference. Dates change only for a compelling reason, sought by letter detailing the basis, all counsel’s positions, and the delay sought. Settlement talks, “summer months,” other cases, and lack of diligent discovery are not compelling. Moving trial or the dispositive motion deadline is considered only in extraordinary circumstances.

docs.t: Judge Jerry Pappert (E.D. Pa.) — Discovery
docs.x: Judge Jerry Pappert, E.D. Pa.. Discovery: Standard-track discovery is usually 90 to 120 days from the Rule 16 conference; raise any need for more time at a conference. Routine disputes go to a telephone conference after a reasonable effort to resolve them; the judge may first require a joint letter. A motion to compel that follows is capped at 5 double-spaced pages in 12-point font (motion and memorandum together), with a 5-page response within 5 days. Sanctions may go to the prevailing party. Telephone rulings are available during depositions that would otherwise have to be adjourned. Lay opinion evidence under FRE 701 on liability or damages must be disclosed with supporting documents by the expert-report deadline.

docs.t: Judge Jerry Pappert (E.D. Pa.) — Protective orders and sealing (trap)
docs.x: Judge Jerry Pappert, E.D. Pa.. Protective orders and sealing (trap): Protective orders and confidentiality agreements are approved only where absolutely necessary and for good cause, and must include the language: “the court reserves its inherent power to modify the terms of this agreement and permit the disclosure of information where the interest of justice so requires.” A confidentiality designation does not mean filings will be sealed; the party must show the interest in secrecy outweighs public access (Gratz Coll. v. Synergis). Pro hac vice motions without the fee are denied; admitted counsel must register for CM/ECF within 7 days.

docs.t: Judge Jerry Pappert (E.D. Pa.) — Injunctions, settlement, and arbitration
docs.x: Judge Jerry Pappert, E.D. Pa.. Injunctions, settlement, and arbitration: TRO and preliminary injunction requests are listed promptly; the judge may hold a pre-hearing conference and require proposed findings and conclusions before the hearing. The Scheduling Order refers cases to a magistrate judge for settlement; the judge does not take part in settlement talks in non-jury cases. Arbitration-track cases get no Rule 16 conference or Scheduling Order unless there is a de novo appeal; finish discovery before the arbitration hearing, after which discovery and dispositive motions are ordinarily not allowed.

docs.t: Judge Jerry Pappert (E.D. Pa.) — Pretrial memoranda (trap)
docs.x: Judge Jerry Pappert, E.D. Pa.. Pretrial memoranda (trap): Beyond L.R. 16.1(c), include all stipulations; particularized objections to authenticity, admissibility (other than relevance), expert qualifications, and FRE 701 lay opinion; and case-in-chief deposition designations by page and line with counter-designations. Exhibits should not include pleadings, written discovery responses, or transcripts without a specific reason. Submit one unified, tailored set of jury instructions and one verdict form; on disagreements give competing versions with an explanation. Use Third Circuit models where possible. File on the docket and email Word versions to Chambers_of_Judge_Pappert@paed.uscourts.gov. Raise videotaped-deposition objections with the pretrial memoranda, then edit the tapes per the ruling.

docs.t: Judge Jerry Pappert (E.D. Pa.) — Trial
docs.x: Judge Jerry Pappert, E.D. Pa.. Trial: Submit one agreed set of voir dire questions 7 days before trial; the judge conducts voir dire and allows suggested follow-ups. Jurors may take notes. No trial briefs unless requested. Motions in limine: 5-page briefs, no replies, timing set in the Scheduling Order. One joint, pre-marked exhibit book with exhibit list; give the court 2 copies at the final pretrial conference. A witness may not testify about an exhibit’s content before it is admitted unless the parties agree. Aim for openings under 30 minutes and closings under 45. Only one lawyer per side per witness, opening, or closing. Examine from the lectern or counsel table. Rule 50 and 52(c) motions must be in writing. An unavailable witness’s deposition must be used; unavailability will not delay trial. During deliberations, stay within 10 minutes of the courthouse. These pretrial and trial p

docs.t: Judge Joel Harvey Slomsky (E.D. Pa.) — Communicating with chambers (trap)
docs.x: Judge Joel Harvey Slomsky, E.D. Pa.. Communicating with chambers (trap): Written communication must be by filing. Letters are allowed only when the court requests one, for an uncontested continuance of Rule 16 deadlines that doesn’t affect the summary judgment or trial dates, for an unanticipated personal matter affecting counsel’s participation, or to report settlement or dismissal, and must state whether counsel agrees or disagrees. Don’t copy the court on correspondence between counsel; no faxes. Law clerks can’t give advice or grant continuances; don’t call them unless they call you. Phone the courtroom deputy only when writing can’t timely address scheduling, witness, exhibit, video-replay, or discovery-call arrangements.

docs.x: Judge Joel Harvey Slomsky, E.D. Pa.. Courtesy copies and motions (trap): Send chambers two courtesy copies of every motion and related briefs, even though filed on ECF. docs.x: Judge Joel Harvey Slomsky, E.D. Pa.. Pending motions don’t excuse the meeting or report; noncompliant parties have no voice at the conference and may be sanctioned. Lead trial counsel, not an associate, must attend, with thorough knowledge of the facts and client authority to discuss all claims, defenses, and settlement. File motions to dismiss, amend, transfer, add parties, and other threshold motions before the Rule 16 conference, and be ready to argue them there. The report form expects discovery to close 120–150 days after the Rule 16 conference, simultaneous expert reports, an explanation of any decision not to pursue early ADR, and

docs.t: Judge Joel Harvey Slomsky (E.D. Pa.) — Discovery
docs.x: Judge Joel Harvey Slomsky, E.D. Pa.. Discovery: Rule 26(a) disclosures are due within 14 days of the order scheduling the Rule 16 conference, and discovery must start immediately on notice of that conference; pending motions don’t excuse it. Expect to report progress at the conference. For disputes, comply with Local Rule 26.1(f) with a certification detailing efforts to resolve; telephone conferences are encouraged, and a discovery motion may be decided before any response is filed. If the parties can’t agree on e-discovery, the default Order Governing Electronic Discovery applies (liaisons, sequenced searches, image-file production, a retention agreement within 30 days, and a statement of compliance within 7 days of identifying custodians).

docs.t: Judge Joel Harvey Slomsky (E.D. Pa.) — Summary judgment
docs.x: Judge Joel Harvey Slomsky, E.D. Pa.. Summary judgment: The motion must include a separate Statement of Undisputed Facts in numbered paragraphs limited to facts bearing on dispositive material issues. The opposition responds paragraph by paragraph and adds any further facts in separate numbered paragraphs; facts not controverted are admitted. Every fact must cite the specific record source, with page and line for documents and depositions.

docs.t: Judge Joel Harvey Slomsky (E.D. Pa.) — Settlement, ADR, and confidentiality orders
docs.x: Judge Joel Harvey Slomsky, E.D. Pa.. Settlement, ADR, and confidentiality orders: Counsel must attend a settlement conference with the magistrate judge named in the scheduling order (the document names Magistrate Judge Carol Sandra Moore Wells), with parties or persons with full settlement authority unless excused in advance. Stipulated confidentiality or sealing orders need a detailed good-cause statement (Pansy) and must include, or substantially track: “The Court retains the right to allow disclosure of any subject covered by this stipulation or to modify this stipulation at any time in the interest of justice.”

docs.x: Judge Joel Harvey Slomsky, E.D. Pa.. Final pretrial conference (trap): The Local Rule 16.1(c) pretrial memorandum must detail the substance of each witness’s testimony; labeling testimony “liability” or “damages” is not enough. Bring one copy of each exhibit and three copies of an exhibit schedule; at trial provide two copies of each exhibit, numbered consecutively in a single tabbed three-ring binder. The conference lasts 2–4 hours and is meant to resolve all evidentiary issues: confer first and come ready to argue remaining objections. Written deposition objections (page and line, basis, highlighted transcript) are due before the conference; video-deposition disputes at least 10 days before it. Cases in the trial pool must be ready to start on 48 hours’ notice.

docs.t: Judge Joel Harvey Slomsky (E.D. Pa.) — Civil trial
docs.x: Judge Joel Harvey Slomsky, E.D. Pa.. Civil trial: Counsel conduct civil voir dire (generally 30 minutes per side) after resolving disputed questions; the judge conducts criminal voir dire. No speaking objections (state a rule number or one-word basis); sidebars are rarely allowed. One attorney per witness or legal point. Rebuttal is limited to 5 minutes and may not rehash closing. Lay opinion support under FRE 701 must be disclosed when expert reports are due. Submit joint substantive jury instructions and verdict forms only (no basic instructions); failure to cooperate draws sanctions. Disputed instructions need authority, and modified model instructions show additions underlined and deletions bracketed. Non-jury cases: agreed and proposed findings and conclusions at least 7 days before trial. Jurors generally may not take notes and generally don’t get written instructions. Counsel must

docs.t: Judge Joel Harvey Slomsky (E.D. Pa.) — Criminal cases (trap)
docs.x: Judge Joel Harvey Slomsky, E.D. Pa.. Criminal cases (trap): No continuance issues until the defendant signs and dockets the court’s Speedy Trial Act Acknowledgment of Rights form. Suppression, Starks, and Daubert hearings are typically at least 2 weeks before trial, and the government must file proposed findings and conclusions before the hearing. Pretrial conferences are held only in complex or multi-attorney cases. Proposed points for charge and jury interrogatories are due 7 days before trial, each numbered on a separate sheet with authority. The government’s trial memorandum (elements, facts, witnesses and their testimony, legal issues) is due 1 week before trial; its guilty plea memorandum at least 2 days before the change-of-plea hearing. docs.t: Judge John R. Padova (E.D. Pa.) — Replies need leave; motions ripe on response (trap)
docs.x: Judge John R. Padova, E.D. Pa.. Replies need leave; motions ripe on response (trap): A motion is “ripe” once the response is filed. Replies and surreplies need leave: move within 14 days of the previous filing and attach the proposed brief as an exhibit. A party intending to amend under Rule 15 must file a notice of intent within the 14-day period for responding to a motion to dismiss (L. Civ. R. 7.1(c)). No set days for argument; the judge orders argument or grants a request made in writing in the motion, response, or reply.

docs.t: Judge John R. Padova (E.D. Pa.) — Courtesy copies (trap)
docs.x: Judge John R. Padova, E.D. Pa.. Courtesy copies (trap): Send one courtesy copy of all motion papers to chambers, stapled or neatly bound with dividers between exhibits; the same applies to all Rule 56 materials, motions in limine, and trial briefs. Pretrial memoranda: file one and send 2 copies to chambers. Stipulation of uncontested facts: file the original and send 2 copies to chambers. Jury instructions, verdict forms, voir dire questions, and proposed findings and conclusions also go to chambers in hard copy and by email in Word to chambers_of_judge_john_r_padova@paed.uscourts.gov. Appellate briefs should be emailed to chambers when a decision is appealed.

docs.t: Judge John R. Padova (E.D. Pa.) — Summary judgment
docs.x: Judge John R. Padova, E.D. Pa.. Summary judgment: Except in pro se prisoner cases, the parties must meet and confer about material facts at least 14 days before any Rule 56 motion is filed. The motion must include a Concise Statement of Stipulated Material Facts in numbered paragraphs, with record citations when possible. Any party relying on other facts must file a numbered Concise Statement of Additional Facts citing the precise pages of the record. A pending Rule 56 motion does not stay Scheduling Order deadlines; seek any extension by letter or motion.

docs.t: Judge John R. Padova (E.D. Pa.) — Contact and correspondence
docs.x: Judge John R. Padova, E.D. Pa.. Contact and correspondence: Phone inquiries go to Deputy Malissa Wolenski, (215) 597-1178; communication with law clerks is strongly discouraged. All filings must be on ECF. Letters are allowed only for transmittals, court-requested information, continuing the preliminary pretrial conference, uncontested Rule 16 deadline extensions not affecting trial, personal matters affecting counsel’s participation, or reporting a settlement or disposition. Everything else must be filed. Telephone conferences (arranged through the deputy) are used for non-complex pretrial, scheduling, discovery, and settlement matters; discuss the issue with opposing counsel first, and all parties must be on the call. Pro hac vice requires a written motion on or before counsel’s first appearance.

docs.t: Judge John R. Padova (E.D. Pa.) — Preliminary pretrial conference
docs.x: Judge John R. Padova, E.D. Pa.. Preliminary pretrial conference: Usually set within 30 days after all defendants answer. Hold the Rule 26(f) meeting at least 14 days before; parties who don’t comply have no voice at the conference and may be sanctioned. At least 3 business days before, submit to chambers (not docketed) the completed Scheduling Information Report and the Rule 26(f) discovery plan. The report covers Rule 26(a) disclosures, readiness for trial, settlement timing, expected dispositive motions, trial time, and reasons for any discovery period over 4 months. Counsel must have client authority on all subjects including settlement, and be ready to argue any pending motions.

docs.t: Judge John R. Padova (E.D. Pa.) — Continuances and extensions (trap)
docs.x: Judge John R. Padova, E.D. Pa.. Continuances and extensions (trap): Original dates hold unless a compelling reason is shown, before the date runs; this covers briefing, argument, hearings, discovery, and trial. Requests go by letter or formal motion, and agreed stipulations still need court approval. Letters suffice only for uncontested Rule 16 deadline extensions not affecting trial date or pool placement, continuing the preliminary pretrial conference, or uncontested extensions to respond to a motion.

docs.t: Judge John R. Padova (E.D. Pa.) — Discovery and confidentiality
docs.x: Judge John R. Padova, E.D. Pa.. Discovery and confidentiality: Discovery usually runs 60 to 90 days from the initial conference. Disputes are preferably handled by telephone conference; if unresolved, file a motion to compel. A motion to compel after a discovery default is usually granted on presentation under L. Civ. R. 26.1(g). Confidentiality orders are entered only on a specific good-cause finding under Pansy v. Borough of Stroudsburg; private confidentiality agreements are allowed. Expert testimony is limited at trial to what was disclosed (CV and Rule 26(a)(2)(B) information) by the scheduling order dates, except for good cause.

docs.t: Judge John R. Padova (E.D. Pa.) — Settlement, arbitration, and injunctions
docs.x: Judge John R. Padova, E.D. Pa.. Settlement, arbitration, and injunctions: The judge takes an active role in settlement, typically starting at the initial conference, and may hold an early settlement conference with parties or corporate principals present. Non-jury cases are usually referred to a magistrate judge for settlement. Damages are presumed not to exceed the $150,000 arbitration limit unless timely certified otherwise (L. Civ. R. 53.2.3(C)). After a trial de novo demand, expect a standard scheduling order, ordinarily no new discovery, and trial within 30 days. For TROs and injunctions, the judge usually holds a conference before scheduling a hearing and handles expedited discovery by phone.

docs.t: Judge John R. Padova (E.D. Pa.) — Scheduling order and pretrial memoranda (trap)
docs.x: Judge John R. Padova, E.D. Pa.. Scheduling order and pretrial memoranda (trap): Trial gets a date certain, and the Scheduling Order is the only written notice of it; counsel are attached as of that date. docs.t: Judge Debra C. Poplin (E.D. Tenn.) — Settlement and civility
docs.x: Judge Debra C. Poplin, E.D. Tenn.. Settlement and civility: Parties are expected to mediate in good faith before trial; those who will not must be ready to explain why the case is unsuitable. On settlement, promptly file a Notice of Settlement, then a stipulation or agreed order of dismissal within 30 days or before the trial date, whichever is sooner (L.R. 68.1). The court places the utmost importance on civility toward the court, opposing counsel, and witnesses.

docs.t: Judge J. Ronnie Greer (E.D. Tenn.) — Scheduling and continuances (trap)
docs.x: Judge J. Ronnie Greer, E.D. Tenn.. Scheduling and continuances (trap): Judge Greer generally does not hold in-person scheduling conferences; the scheduling order is entered from the parties’ Rule 26(f) Report (file a request if you want a conference). Trial is usually set about 18 months after the report, almost always on a Tuesday, in Greeneville regardless of division. Objections to the scheduling order, including the trial date, are due within 10 days of entry. After that, continuances and extensions are granted only in extraordinary circumstances, and agreed orders changing deadlines will not be entered. A pending dispositive motion does not stay the case or discovery unless the court grants a motion to stay for good cause. Court-ordered mediation does not move the trial date or deadlines.

docs.t: Judge J. Ronnie Greer (E.D. Tenn.) — Motions and briefing (trap)
docs.x: Judge J. Ronnie Greer, E.D. Tenn.. Motions and briefing (trap): Requests to exceed Local Rule 7.1(b) page limits are rarely granted. No courtesy copies are required or wanted. Oral argument is decided case by case; include a formal request in your filing. Failing to respond to any motion, dispositive or not, may be deemed a waiver of opposition. In the form order, motions to amend or add parties are due at T – 60 weeks, Rule 12(c) motions at T – 56 weeks, and dispositive motions at T – 30 weeks.

docs.t: Judge J. Ronnie Greer (E.D. Tenn.) — Summary judgment (trap)
docs.x: Judge J. Ronnie Greer, E.D. Tenn.. Summary judgment (trap): A Rule 56 motion must include a separate concise statement of material facts in numbered paragraphs, each with a specific record citation. The opponent responds to each fact (undisputed, undisputed for the motion only, or disputed with a specific record citation) and may add numbered additional disputed facts; the movant may reply to those within the Local Rules’ reply time. Noncompliant statements may be struck sua sponte, likely without a second chance.

docs.t: Judge J. Ronnie Greer (E.D. Tenn.) — Communications
docs.x: Judge J. Ronnie Greer, E.D. Tenn.. Communications: Letters are discouraged except on minor uncontested matters, copied to all counsel; contested matters require a motion. Do not copy the court on correspondence between counsel. Counsel may speak with law clerks but not about the merits. Telephone conferences are encouraged for all matters; schedule through the assigned law clerk.

docs.t: Judge J. Ronnie Greer (E.D. Tenn.) — Discovery and experts (trap)
docs.x: Judge J. Ronnie Greer, E.D. Tenn.. Discovery and experts (trap): Discovery generally runs 6 to 8 months and closes at T – 43 weeks; serve requests early enough for responses to fall before the cut-off. Disputes are handled by telephone conference after a good-faith effort to resolve them. Expert disclosures: plaintiff T – 56 weeks, defendant T – 51 weeks. All objections to expert qualifications or testimony (F.R.E. 701–706 and Daubert) are due at T – 47 weeks, the same day as the joint mediation notice. A written status report is due at T – 56 weeks; missing it triggers an in-person status conference.

docs.t: Judge J. Ronnie Greer (E.D. Tenn.) — Exhibits, depositions, and motions in limine (trap)
docs.x: Judge J. Ronnie Greer, E.D. Tenn.. Exhibits, depositions, and motions in limine (trap): By T – 9 weeks, exchange exhibit lists, deposition designations, witness lists, and damages lists, and produce exhibits for inspection, marked with Greeneville clerk’s office stickers bearing the case number (defense numbers continue after plaintiff’s). Evidence depositions must also be done by then. Any objection to authenticity or admissibility must be made by motion in limine, or it is admitted. Motions in limine are due T – 7 weeks (responses T – 5 weeks) and may be heard by the magistrate judge; no depositions after that date. Dispositive motions in limine may be summarily denied.

docs.t: Judge J. Ronnie Greer (E.D. Tenn.) — Pretrial order and conference
docs.x: Judge J. Ronnie Greer, E.D. Tenn.. Pretrial order and conference: Plaintiff serves a draft pretrial order 45 days before the final pretrial conference (47 if by mail); defendant responds within 5 working days. If the parties cannot agree after a face-to-face conference, plaintiff notifies chambers at least 20 days before; failure may mean dismissal for failure to prosecute. File the proposed order 5 days before the conference (T – 4 weeks). Bring all marked exhibits to the final pretrial conference; any not produced cannot be used at trial. Disclose courtroom technology at least 5 days before the conference. No later than 7 days before trial, file final witness and exhibit lists, damages list, deposition designations, expert résumés, proposed jury instructions (foreseeable instructions not submitted may be summarily denied), and a proposed verdict form (joint preferred). docs.t: Judge J. Ronnie Greer (E.D. Tenn.) — Trial
docs.x: Judge J. Ronnie Greer, E.D. Tenn.. Trial: Trial starts at 9 a.m.; cases not reached are held in line for up to 10 available days. Parties who settle on the trial date are charged jury costs. Submit electronic exhibits for JERS to the courtroom deputy by T – 1 week (strongly encouraged). Counsel conduct voir dire in civil cases (the judge does preliminary voir dire in criminal cases); no back-striking. One attorney per witness; examine per Local Rule 83.3. Sidebars are discouraged, and examination beyond redirect and recross is generally not permitted. Bench issues: proposed findings and conclusions, with citations to trial testimony and evidence, are due within 10 days after trial; post-trial briefs generally within 10 days. During deliberations, be able to return within 10 minutes.

docs.t: Judge J. Ronnie Greer (E.D. Tenn.) — Injunctions and ADR
docs.x: Judge J. Ronnie Greer, E.D. Tenn.. Injunctions and ADR: TROs and preliminary injunctions follow Rule 65 with no special procedure; sufficient expedited discovery is generally allowed. Do not send appellate filings to the judge. The judge will generally order mediation under Local Rule 16.4 if the parties do not agree to it; a joint notice that the case is unsuitable must give reasons.

docs.t: Judge Jill E. McCook (E.D. Tenn.) — Conferences and communications
docs.x: Judge Jill E. McCook, E.D. Tenn.. Conferences and communications: Initial scheduling and pretrial conferences are in person; case management conferences may be by phone. The page says the initial scheduling conference is in person, though the form orders recite a telephonic one. For conference calls, the parties initiate the call to chambers; with more than two lines, set up the conference among yourselves first or give chambers a call-in number and code. Use a land line and handset rather than a speakerphone when possible. Letters are accepted for procedural or settlement information, copied to opposing counsel; any request for an order must be by written motion. Contact with law clerks is acceptable.

docs.t: Judge Jill E. McCook (E.D. Tenn.) — Motions
docs.x: Judge Jill E. McCook, E.D. Tenn.. Motions: Oral argument is preferred. Courtesy copies are wanted for “last minute” filings. Requests to exceed Local Rule 7.1(b) page limits may be made by conference call or written motion. Pro hac vice admission generally requires no hearing.

docs.t: Judge Jill E. McCook (E.D. Tenn.) — Discovery disputes (trap)
docs.x: Judge Jill E. McCook, E.D. Tenn.. Discovery disputes (trap): Per the page, procedural disputes may be handled by conference call, but substantive ones (for example, privilege claims) go by written motion and in-court hearing. Per the form orders, meet and confer first, then email mccook_chambers@tned.uscourts.gov, copying all counsel, to set an informal conference (in court or by phone). Only if it remains unresolved may a written motion be filed, with any Rule 37(a)(1) certification; motions that skip these steps may be summarily denied. Discovery in a standard case usually runs 8 to 10 months, with counsel helping set the schedule; the trial date is set at the initial scheduling conference.

docs.t: Judge Jill E. McCook (E.D. Tenn.) — Form scheduling order deadlines
docs.x: Judge Jill E. McCook, E.D. Tenn.. Form scheduling order deadlines: The posted form orders count back from trial: plaintiff’s experts 32 weeks, defendant’s 28 weeks, rebuttal 25 weeks; amendment/joinder 29 weeks; discovery (including expert depositions) and a joint mediation-suitability report 22 weeks; motions to compel 21 weeks; dispositive and Daubert motions 16 weeks; motions in limine 30 days; final pretrial conference 2 weeks. Untimely dispositive motions and motions to compel may be summarily denied. A written agreement to extend discovery does not move other deadlines, and the court will not take up disputes arising after the discovery deadline absent extraordinary circumstances. If the trial date changes, dates not expressly tied to it stay in place.

docs.t: Judge Jill E. McCook (E.D. Tenn.) — Experts and motions in limine (trap)
docs.x: Judge Jill E. McCook, E.D. Tenn.. Experts and motions in limine (trap): Challenges to an expert’s qualifications or testimony under Federal Rules of Evidence 701–706 and Daubert are due by the dispositive motion deadline (16 weeks before trial). The court will not entertain a motion to exclude expert testimony styled as a motion in limine. Motions in limine (on exhibits, depositions, and non-expert witnesses, with authority) are due 30 days before trial; responses within 7 days. They may be addressed at the final pretrial conference.
